News.title: Harvey Nichols bought by owner of Sports Direct
News.content:
Luxury department store Harvey Nichols has been bought by the owner of Sports Direct, which warned a "significant restructuring" was needed to ensure the 200-year-old business remains sustainable.

Mike Ashley's Frasers Group will take control of the Harvey Nichols stores, including its flagship in Knightsbridge, as well as the international franchise.

The department store was immortalised in BBC sitcom Absolutely Fabulous, but had faced challenges in recent years. The firm had appointed administrators in June.

Michael Murray, Frasers' chief executive and Ashley's son-in-law, called the store a "British institution with significant potential" but added "clear meaningful change is needed".

"The turnaround will require tough choices and we are prepared to make those decisions, even if that means a smaller business in the near term, to create a stronger and more sustainable Harvey Nichols for the long-term," he said.

Harvey Nichols carries more than 800 premium and luxury brands and has over 1,000 employees. Its other stores are located in Manchester, Birmingham, Bristol, Leeds and Edinburgh.

Frasers Group will also acquire the online business, and shops will continue to operate under their existing licensing.

Earlier this week, Harvey Nichols warned in its latest accounts that it would need to "cease trading" within a year if it failed to secure new investment.

It had faced "sustained trading and operational challenges" recently and Frasers Group said it will need to conduct a review of the store's portfolio, structure and cost base.

A recent auction for the store saw Frasers battle retail rival Next to take control of the firm.

Harvey Nichols was bought in 1991 by Hong Kong-based businessman Sir Dickson Poon but he put the group up for sale earlier this year.

News.title: Ski Sunday host Chemmy Alcott suffers collapsed lung after jumping into lake
News.content:
Ski Sunday presenter Chemmy Alcott says she suffered a collapsed lung after jumping into a lake while on holiday in France.

The 44-year-old former GB Olympic skier posted a clip on Instagram, external that showed her jumping off a five metre platform into Lake Annecy, in the French Alps, before landing badly and ending up in hospital.

"Most people badly time a front flip off a five-metre platform and get winded," she said in the clip.

"I apparently don't do things by halves. Collapsed lung, chest drain and a very expensive lesson in rotation."

Alcott explained that she initially went back to jump again after her difficult landing, out of "embarassment" and "just so I wasn't making a big deal out of it".

But she soon realised she "couldn't breathe properly and should probably go and get it checked out".

She later shared images of herself in hospital with tubes and wires sticking out of her body.

In the caption to the main clip - titled "this didn't end well" - she wrote: "Well... that escalated quickly. Turns out five metres is quite a long way to discover you've got the rotation wrong.

"One badly timed front flip. One very hard landing. One collapsed lung. One chest drain. And a few more hospital overnights than were on the holiday itinerary...

"I absolutely loved Annecyâ¦ but I'm not entirely sure it loved me back."

A collapsed lung - medically known as a pneumothorax - occurs when air becomes trapped in the space between the lung and the chest wall, according the NHS.

News.title: Met chief accepts mistakes made over Simon Levy but defends investigation into murders
News.content:
The head of the Metropolitan Police Sir Mark Rowley has defended the force's investigation into double murderer Simon Levy.

Levy was on bail and being monitored by police when he murdered Carmenza Valencia-Trujillo in March 2025 and Sheryl Wilkins five months later, as well as violently raping a third woman.

Sir Mark acknowledged mistakes over the force's handling of Levy, but said suggestions it had not tried to build a case over his first murder were "just not true", following criticism including from Labour MP Jess Phillips.

He told BBC Radio 4's Today programme that detectives had done "serious" work but "didn't have enough evidence" for a charge.

The Met did not seek a charging decision from the Crown Prosecution Service (CPS) over Valencia-Trujillo's murder until after Wilkins had been killed.

The police and CPS has apologised over a series of decisions that left the convicted sex offender free to attack the women.

The Independent Office for Police Conduct (IOPC) is currently examining how Levy, 40, was managed over the four-year period from his first conviction in September 2021 for sexual assault up to his final arrest in September 2025.

At the Old Bailey on Wednesday, he was given a whole life prison sentence, meaning he will never be released.

Speaking on BBC Radio 4's Today programme, Sir Mark - who on Wednesday called the case a "whole system failing" - said he had already apologised for what the Met had got wrong.

It emerged after Levy's conviction that the Met did not class Valencia-Trujillo's death in March 2025 as a murder, or pass the case to specialist homicide detectives, until after he had killed again.

Sir Mark said "the public debate needs to be better informed" because "the facts on that are much more complex than people want to acknowledge".

He said that while Valencia-Trujillo's death was "clearly very suspicious and concerning", a pathologist was unable to determine a cause of death and the force "didn't have enough evidence to get to a charge".

Sir Mark added it was only after the murder of Wilkins that the Met had the "combined evidence" to move forward.

"So the inference that the Met didn't try on that case is just not true, the Met tried," he said.

However, the Met did not ask the CPS for advice about Valencia-Trujillo's death, let alone a charging decision, until after the murder of Wilkins, the BBC has previously reported.

The fact there was no formal cause of death would not have prevented the case being taken on by specialist homicide detectives, who are skilled at building murder cases even when there is not a formal cause of death.

Levy's semen was on Valencia-Trujillo and his blood was at the murder scene. CCTV that showed Levy in the area, walking in the same direction as Valencia-Trujillo shortly after she passed a camera, was not viewed by the local team despite being gathered.

Other possible relevant CCTV was never gathered, and had been deleted by the time the specialist murder team took over months later.

In that case, the local team investigating the death did not engage with the Met's specialist murder teams apart from the day her body was discovered in March 2025.

A specialist homicide team attended the crime scene that day and recommended the case stay with local officers pending further enquiries, but there was no further contact until after Wilkins was murdered in August.

News.title: Heatwaves drive A&E attendances up to record high
News.content:
England's A&Es are experiencing their busiest period ever, with the record-breaking heat cited as a key factor.

More than 2.4 million patients attended emergency departments each month for May, June and July â the three highest monthly totals recorded in history.

NHS bosses say the pressure has been as bad as it is in winter months. The extreme heat has caused people to fall ill with dehydration and heatstroke, and has increased the risk of complications for those with heart, kidney and respiratory problems.

It comes as unions warn staff are being forced to work in inhumane conditions because of the heat, with reports of some collapsing and others having seizures.

The problems have been further complicated by equipment, including scanners and IT systems, breaking down.

NHS medical director Prof Frankie Swords praised the "outstanding professionalism" of staff and said the situation was making delivering care challenging.

She advised: "With temperatures peaking today, please take sensible precautions to stay safe - keep hydrated, avoid the sun during the hottest part of the day, especially if you are clinically vulnerable, and check in on older or vulnerable friends, relatives and neighbours."

News.title: Boy suffered fatal brain injury in seaside drowning
News.content:
A seven-year-old boy suffered a fatal brain injury after he got into difficulty off the Essex coast, a coroner has said.

Musa Ahmed died six days after the incident in West Mersea, in which his 15-year-old cousin, Sameeha Rahman, and her mother, Shelina, 41, also died.

They were all enjoying a day out to the island, near Colchester, from east London when the tragedy unfolded on 22 July.

Their provisional causes of death were all given as drowning at an inquest opening in Chelmsford, while Musa also died from a hypoxic ischaemic brain injury.

"Clearly it is so tragic to come across the death of any individual," said Lincoln Brookes, the senior coroner for Essex.

"But when three occur at the same time and all from the same family, one cannot understand the tragic nature of such an incident."

Three others were taken to hospital by ambulance after the incident and are said to be recovering.

News.title: Three death row killers to be executed on same day in three different states
News.content:

Read our Privacy notice

Three men in different states are set for lethal injection on Thursday in a rare collections of executions on the same day.

The last time three executions were held on the same day was January 7, 2010, when Louisiana, Ohio and Texas put inmates to death. Three executions were scheduled on the same day in 2018, but only one went forward after a Texas man was granted a reprieve and prison officials in Alabama had problems with the IV line.

The latest case sees a man in Tennessee faces execution for killing a motel maid. An Oklahoma man is scheduled to die for killing his girlfriend. And an Alabama man will be put to death after dropping all his appeals in the killing of a 5-year-old girl he paid her mother to abuse.

Eleven states carried out executions in 2025 in the U.S. If the Tennessee and Alabama deaths take place, six states will have had executions in 2026.

Florida executed two men on the same day in July and has put 31 prisoners to death since the start of 2025.

open image in gallery Anthony Darrell Hines ( Tennessee Department of Correction )

Tennessee plans to execute Anthony Darrell Hines for the 1985 murder of Catherine Jean Jenkins.

Hines stabbed Jenkins to death while the 54-year-old was working as a motel maid in Kingston Springs. He was sentenced to death in 1986, won an appeal for a new sentencing hearing and was again sentenced to death in 1989.

Hines' execution date comes just three months after the attempted lethal injection of another man was called off because of a problem inserting an IV.

Hines, 66, appealed unsuccessfully to the governor and the courts, saying that the doctor who oversaw the May execution was unqualified and likely to botch his execution as well. He said his thinness and muscular atrophy after two strokes mean he could face problems with an IV as well.

During the attempted execution of Tony Carruthers, the IV team established a primary line right away but then worked for more than an hour trying to insert a backup line. Carruthers' lawyer witnessed the attempts and said the team tried to insert an IV in Carruthers’ arm, hand and foot before attempting to insert a central line.

In the end, Gov. Bill Lee called off the execution and gave Carruthers a one-year reprieve.

The state has declined to say whether the same doctor will preside over Hines’ execution. Regardless, the Tennessee Supreme Court ruled Hines had not proven the doctor was unqualified and suggested the problems were an isolated mishap.

open image in gallery Jeremy Williams ( Alabama Department of Corrections )

Alabama is scheduled to execute Jeremy Williams by lethal injection for the 2021 rape and murder of a 5-year-old Georgia girl.

Williams, who pleaded guilty to killing Kamarie Holland, declined to appeal and asked for his death sentence to be carried out.

Williams, 42, raped and strangled Holland after offering her mother $2,500 for the child to perform a sex act, prosecutors said.

Williams filmed his attack on the girl and kept her body to continue to abuse, prosecutors said.

“To see on video what he did to this baby, what a grown man could do to a child, it’s shocking, it’s horrible, it’s disgusting,” Russell County District Attorney Richard Chancey said. “It’s just a level of evil.”

Williams also was a suspect in the 2005 death of his infant daughter in Alaska but charges were not filed until 2022.

Corey Holland, Kamarie’s father, said his daughter was an exuberant 5-year-old who loved princesses and made people laugh.

“She loved playing dress-up, all her little Halloween costumes and her princess stuff I got her. She liked anything girly,” Corey Holland said.

It will be Alabama’s first execution of the year if it goes forward. A nitrogen gas execution was halted in June after a federal judge ruled the method unconstitutional.

The girl's mother is serving a 20-year prison sentence after pleading guilty to sex trafficking.

open image in gallery Carlos Cuesta-Rodriguez, ( AP )

A man convicted of fatally shooting his girlfriend at their Oklahoma City home in 2003 said he regrets killing her and didn't ask a board for clemency.

Carlos Cuesta-Rodriguez, 70, is set to die by lethal injection at the state’s penitentiary in rural McAlester. He would be the third person put to death this year in Oklahoma and the 20th under Republican Gov. Kevin Stitt, who leaves office in January after eight years.

Olimpia Fisher, 43, planned to leave Cuesta-Rodriguez when he shot her in one eye and then waited about eight minutes as she screamed for help before firing the fatal shot into her other eye.

“He made her suffer because she dared to live beyond his control,” Oklahoma Attorney General Gentner Drummond told the state’s Pardon and Parole Board on July 14.

Last month, the board voted 3-1 against recommending clemency for Cuesta-Rodriguez. His attorneys had asked the board to recommend he serve life in prison, saying he had a difficult childhood in Cuba and suffered from brain damage, post-traumatic stress disorder and major depression with psychotic episodes.

Former boxer Prichard Colon has died at the age of 33, 11 years after he famously fell into a coma following a controversial loss.

Colon’s father took to social media to share the news on Thursday.

“Good morning, my people,” Colon’s father Richard wrote on Facebook. “I regret to inform you of the passing of my son Prichard from this earthly world. Now he is in a better world.

“I did everything possible to fulfil his wish, his dream of bringing him on vacation to Puerto Rico as much as he desired, but couldn’t. “Thank you for so many years of love and prayers. As much as you can, please keep us in your prayers.”

Colon was 16-0 (13 KOs) before his infamous fight with Terrel Williams in 2015.

In that bout, Colon appeared to be struck in the back of the head numerous times with illegal punches. Colon informed the referee, but the bout continued. Colon was later docked two points for a low blow.

The Puerto Rican was floored in the ninth round, and confusion thereafter saw his corner team remove his gloves, believing the fight was over. Instead, Colon was disqualified.

Colon was helped to his changing room, where he vomited and collapsed. He was then taken to hospital, where he was diagnosed with a subdural haematoma.

He underwent an emergency operation to reduce brain swelling and evacuate the haematoma. Subsequently, he fell into a coma which lasted 221 days.

Once Colon emerged from the coma, he remained in a vegetative state and was unable to speak without computer assistance.

Attorney General Todd Blanche sought to rally a depleted Justice Department workforce Thursday in his first speech since taking the reins of the beleaguered agency, promising rank-and-file staff that he will lead them with integrity.

Blanche's speech inside the storied Great Hall at Justice Department headquarters represented an effort to reassure lawyers and law enforcement officials on the heels of a tumultuous confirmation battle that exposed deep concerns about the direction of the agency under Republican President Donald Trump.

Blanche vowed to uphold the rule of law “without fear or favor,” and told staff he would welcome their ideas and encourage disagreement. Without mentioning specific moves that have raised alarms from critics that Blanche is still functioning as Trump’s personal lawyer, the attorney general acknowledged he would “not get every decision right.”

“Everything that I do will not be the right path or the right decision,” said Blanche, who served as Trump's criminal defense lawyer before entering the department last year as deputy attorney general. “No one does that, but I do promise you this: I promise you that I will work as hard as any of you. I promise that I’ll listen to you. That I will listen to the ideas that you have, or adjustments that we need to make, and if we need to make them, I will make them.”

Blanche is assuming control of the Justice Department at a turbulent time, with mass firings and resignations having hollowed out the workforce and a slew of politically charged investigations drawing concerns that the agency is being used as a weapon to target the president's perceived foes.

He was confirmed by the Senate early Saturday by the narrowest of margins, opposed by two Republicans who expressed concerns about what they described as the politicization of the Justice Department under Trump.

Blanche told the workforce he is proud of the department's work under the second Trump administration to tackle violent crime, illegal drug trafficking and violent gangs and cartels.

"It’s easy to focus on the negative or the news story that is critical of something we’re doing or something that we’ve done, or questions something that we're doing or something that we've done," Blanche said. “But do not forget that we have accomplished a tremendous amount of good, positive work in the past year and a half.”

American forces were overwhelmed by Ukrainian drones during a training exercise that exposed U.S. military vulnerabilities — which have also been exploited to deadly effect by Iran, according to a new report.

Ukraine's drone operators easily spotted and defeated U.S. troops and armored vehicles so quickly that they had to be “re-spawned” and sent back into the field to keep the exercise going, The Wall Street Journal said, citing an unidentified U.S. official who was briefed on the matter.

An entire U.S. armored brigade was reportedly eliminated at one point in the twice-yearly training, which took place in Germany over two weeks in April and May and is called “Combined Resolve.”

Eliot Cohen, a former Pentagon civilian adviser who's now a defense expert at the bipartisan Center for Strategic and International Studies think tank, told the Journal that recent battlefield experience has demonstrated the importance of drones in modern warfare.

“It is vital that the U.S. military master that, and thus far, unfortunately, that does not seem to be the case,” he said.

open image in gallery Recent military training exercises for US forces in Germany show how effectively Ukrainian drone operators, like the one pictured here, perform in combat scenarios ( Getty )

The White House referred an inquiry from The Independent to the Pentagon, which said to contact the military’s European Command. It didn't immediately respond to a request for comment.

A total of 18 U.S. service members have been killed in action since President Donald Trump launched his ongoing war against Iran without congressional approval on Feb. 28.

Six soldiers were killed in an Iranian drone strike against a civilian port in Kuwait the following day, and two others were killed in a July 17 drone and missile attack against an air base in Jordan.

A ninth soldier was killed in what the Pentagon called the "controlled detonation" of a downed Iranian attack drone at an air base in northern Iraq on July 19.

Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth told a Senate committee in mid-May that he'd sent military strategists to Ukraine to study drone combat, after Republican Senator Mitch McConnell of Kentucky referred to the country as the “Silicon Valley of warfare,” The Defense Post reported at the time.

open image in gallery Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth says he’s sent military strategists to Ukraine to study drone warfare ( Getty )

“I’ve personally approved additional personnel there to learn from that drone battlefield, both on offense and defense, to ensure that we’re learning every possible lesson from that conflict and incorporating it in real time into how we defend,” Hegseth testified.

Hegseth also sent a July 10 memo to the military's top brass in which he acknowledged that U.S. forces didn't have “the lethal small drones that the modern battlefield requires” because America had fallen behind in “harnessing technologies we invented but were slow to pursue.”

The joint military exercises in Germany involved about 3,700 U.S troops, mostly from the 3rd Armored Brigade Combat Team, 1st Cavalry Division, who attacked a ground position reinforced by Ukrainian troops, according to the Journal.

The scenario was repeated during the two-week training, and the attacking troops improved their performance as they became more adept at dispersing, concealing themselves and using electronic warfare, an unidentified Army official told the Journal.

The Ukrainians also switched sides midway through the exercises and helped the American soldiers effectively use drones for offensive purposes, the official said.

The U.S. troops were equipped with standard electronic-warfare and counter-drone systems, and new Mobile Brigade Combat teams have fared better in exercises using the latest gear and tactics, the official said.

Training exercises held last year in the Baltic region also resulted in Ukrainian drone operators easily defeating troops from other countries, including the U.K. and Estonia, a person familiar with the matter told the Journal.

In addition, Swedish forces and allied Nato troops were defeated by Ukrainian drone operators during exercises held this past spring, the Journal said, citing Swedish media reports.

Nearly 30 dead small dogfish sharks washed ashore this week along the Jersey shore, and while the discovery may have stunned beachgoers, wildlife officials say the sight is “not unusual.”

Michelle Greenling said she found the sharks while taking a walk Wednesday morning along a stretch of beach in Sea Isle City, New Jersey. She told WPVI that she initially wasn't alarmed by a few dead sharks, but soon found them scattered across about 10 blocks of beach.

"All of a sudden, you start seeing a concentration of small sand sharks, and I thought, 'Well, this is odd,'" Greenling said Wednesday.

Stephen Nagiewicz, a marine scientist at Stockton University, told the outlet that dogfish often travel in schools of hundreds or even thousands, making their presence along the Jersey Shore common, though finding so many dead at once is unusual, he said.

“Couple of things could be: there's something in the water, they got sick and died – That's probably unlikely since people haven't been affected. But more than likely, it was a bycatch for some commercial fishing hatch,” Nagiewicz said about the shocking sighting.

open image in gallery Nearly 30 dead dogfish sharks (similar to the one pictured in this file photo) washed ashore along a New Jersey beach Wednesday, raising questions about what caused the deaths ( AFP/Getty )

WPVI reported Wednesday that it contacted the New Jersey Department of Environmental Protection to ask whether similar shark strandings have been reported elsewhere along the coast, but had not received a response.

On Thursday, a DEP spokesperson told The Independent that the discovery may be less mysterious than it initially appeared. Dogfish and other small sharks commonly move into shallow waters during the summer to forage for food, and some can become trapped inside sandbars when the tide recedes. Those fish may then become stranded and die before the tide returns, the spokesperson said.

They added that the agency is not investigating Wednesday’s discovery because it “does not appear to be an unusual event.”

The DEP spokesperson echoed what Nagiewicz told WPVI, saying summer strandings can happen when the sharks forage close to shore and get caught behind sandbars as the water moves out.

Another possible explanation, the DEP agreed, could be that the sharks may have been caught unintentionally by commercial or recreational fishermen and later discarded as bycatch.

The Independent also contacted the New Jersey Division of Fish and Wildlife for comment.

News.title: Candidates ripped for continuing to take Max Miller’s campaign cash amid domestic violence allegations
News.content:

Whether it's investigating the financials of Elon Musk's pro-Trump PAC or producing our latest documentary, 'The A Word', which shines a light on the American women fighting for reproductive rights, we know how important it is to parse out the facts from the messaging. Democratic candidates for Congress are ripping their Republican opponents for taking money from Rep. Max Miller’s leadership political action committee as he’s become embroiled in a very public dispute with his senator’s-daughter ex-wife.

The attacks come as Miller, who represents Ohio’s 7th congressional district, faces a House Ethics Committee investigation into allegations of domestic violence by ex-wife Emily Moreno, the daughter of Ohio Republican Sen. Bernie Moreno. She has also alleged Miller broke the collarbone of their daughter.

On Wednesday, Emily Moreno also filed a lawsuit against Miller that alleged that he “recklessly” published a nude photograph of their daughter.

Miller has vehemently denied the claims and any wrongdoing and insisted he will stay in the race.

But the heat he’s drawn is now lashing back on fellow Republicans who have received money from Miller’s leadership PAC, Dependable Conservative Leadership PAC. Members often raise money through these committees and disburse it to incumbents in battleground districts and states, as well as challengers.

open image in gallery Rep. Max Miller (R-Ohio) has donated to a slew of Republican incumbents. Some Democrats are hitting their opponents for it. ( Reuters )

In Pennsylvania’s 7th Congressional District, Bob Brooks hit Rep. Ryan Mackenzie for receiving $2,500 from Miller’s committee in March of 2025.

“Ryan Mackenzie is showing his true colors. He took thousands in campaign cash from Max Miller, a congressman facing serious allegations that he violently abused his ex-wife and hurt their young daughter, but Ryan doesn't care,” Brooks spokesman Benny Stanislawski said.

“That's who he is: open for business for whoever's willing to pay up, no questions asked. He's said nothing about whether he'll keep the Miller money. He must apologize and return the money immediately.”

The Independent has reached out to Mackenzie’s campaign for comment.

In addition, in Michigan’s 7th district, Democratic nominee Will Lawrence criticized Rep. Tom Barrett on X for receiving $2,500 from Miller’s PAC in March of 2025.

open image in gallery Rep. Ryan Mackenzie (R-PA) has drawn heat for accepting money from Max Miller’s PAC ( Getty )

“This is who Tom Barrett associates with,” Lawrence posted on X. “He claims to be a family man, but he's taken thousands in campaign cash from a man credibly accused of abusing his ex-wife and daughter. Max Miller shouldn’t be in Congress and Tom Barrett should return this money.”

The Independent has contacted the Barrett campaign for comment.

Both Barrett and Mackenzie won their seats in 2024 in highly-contested races. The Cook Political Report lists both of their contests this November as “Toss Up.” President Donald Trump won both districts.

President Donald Trump has so far publicly stuck with Miller, who worked in his first administration. But other Republicans, including Moreno, have called for his exit from Congress.

open image in gallery Sen. John Husted (R-OH) has called on Miller to drop his reelection bid ( Getty )

Sen. Jon Husted, who also received money from Miller in the past, called on Miller to resign.

“I believe Max would be making the right decision to step aside as a candidate and resign from Congress to focus on what is in the best interest of his daughter,” he said on X. “Years from now, I believe he will look back and know it was the right choice for her.”

Democrats believe that the allegations against Miller could bolster his opponent Brian Poindexter. On Tuesday, the Democratic Congressional Campaign Committee announced Poindexter would be put on the committee’s “Red to Blue program.”

“Brian Poindexter is exactly the kind of leader Ohio families deserve in Congress — a union ironworker who has spent his life working alongside the people he’s running to represent,” Chairwoman Suzan DelBene said in a statement.

“Max Miller has never lived that reality. He bought his way into power, sides with corporate interests over working people, and is now facing credible allegations of domestic violence that cannot be ignored.”

The Cook Political Report rates Ohio’s 7th district as a toss-up.

News.title: ‘More pain’ to come after economic slowdown
News.content:
Thanks for joining me. The economy grew at a slower pace in the second quarter of the year, official figures show, under pressure from the Iran war.

The UK’s gross domestic product (GDP) expanded by 0.4pc between April and June, down from 0.6pc in the first three months of the year, according to the Office for National Statistics.

The figures underline the challenge that the conflict poses for Andy Burnham, who has pledged to deliver “growth in every postcode”.

The Prime Minister has already been warned that the economy will slow further next year if Donald Trump continues his war in the Middle East.

Treasury officials have predicted UK growth of just 0.3pc in 2027 if the Strait of Hormuz stays blocked for the rest of this year.

That is far lower than the 1.6pc predicted by the Office for Budget Responsibility (OBR) in March, based on assumptions made before the start of the war. Here is what you need to know.

5 things to start your day

1) Iran war threatens to cripple growth, Treasury warns Burnham | Officials predict economic expansion of just 0.3pc in 2027 if Strait of Hormuz stays blocked

2) Britain facing £54bn bill for North Sea shutdown | Costs soar amid shortage of specialised ships needed to clear up abandoned oil rigs

3) Ban on zero-hours contracts to cost companies up to £3bn | Businesses face huge bill to offer workers guaranteed hours under Employment Rights Act

4) Nvidia’s AI push has echoes of Enron, says Big Short investor | Michael Burry claims chip giant is engaging in ‘circular’ financing

5) Shadow bank founder battles to stave off bankruptcy threat | Paresh Raja launches legal claim to prevent administrators from chasing him for repayment

What happened overnight

Asian shares were mostly higher, powered by gains for AI-related stocks including computer chips as regional markets tracked a rally on Wall Street.

Japan’s benchmark Nikkei 225 advanced 1.6pc to 68,601.21. In South Korea, the Kospi jumped 4pc, climbing to 6,844.65, as shares in Samsung Electronics surged 5.4pcc. Computer chipmaker SK Hynix jumped 7.1pc.

Hong Kong’s Hang Seng rose 0.3pc to 3,967.28, while the Shanghai Composite index added 0.5pc to 3,967.65.

In Australia, the S&P/ASX 200 slipped 0.4pc to 9,155.80.

Data from the US on Wednesday showed consumer prices had risen in line with analysts’ expectations in July.

Wall Street stocks were boosted on Wednesday by gains made by tech companies CoreWeave and Super Micro Computer, both of which closed up by more than 19pc.

The Nasdaq Composite ended the session up 0.5pc, with the S&P 500 up nearly 0.3pc. The Dow Jones Industrial Average finished the session marginally down.

Oil prices were little changed as investors weighed the deadlock in talks between the US and Iran over the Strait of Hormuz.

Brent crude, the international benchmark, was broadly flat at nearly $89 a barrel.

News.title: H5N1 sparks a very Australian epidemic
News.content:
H5N1 bird flu has reached Australia’s shores and is threatening to infect some of the country’s most unique wildlife.

Australasia is the last continent to be hit by the highly infectious avian influenza H5N1, a new strain of which has been circulating worldwide since 2020.

Since recording its first case in June, more than 200 wild seabirds in Australia have been infected, with fears that the highly infectious flu could quickly ‘jump’ to other species.

While H5N1 has infected animals from foxes to sea lions in other parts of the world in recent years, the epidemic now threatens some of Australia’s most iconic wildlife – many of which are found nowhere else on earth.

An Australian government assessment of more than 2,000 native species warned that nearly one in five faces a high risk from the deadly H5N1 bird flu, with hundreds of unique birds and mammals vulnerable to severe population reductions or even extinction.

Those animals include iconic species like the Tasmanian devils, quolls, and dingoes.

Other aquatic mammals, including the platypus, which is only found in Australia, are at risk of infection through contact with bird droppings in shared wetlands and coastal environments.

News.title: Selfie-seekers bring Man Utd vs Leeds match to premature end
News.content:
Aren’t friendlies supposed to be non-events? Manchester United against Leeds United in Dublin always had the capacity to be lively, but try explaining the half hour that Bruno Fernandes experienced in one breath. It would be impossible.

There was only one player the vast majority of the crowd wanted to see in the grandiosely named Boyle Sports Cup and, in chronological order from his 60th minute introduction, he received a standing ovation, hit the bar, had a goal disallowed, missed a penalty in a shoot-out and lifted a trophy.

Most remarkably – and, certainly, worryingly – of all, he was central to the game being ended early as five young boys, one after the other, breached security and ran to him in the middle of pitch, all of them successfully posing for photos with the Portuguese.

You could say it was harmless fun but it should not have happened and the flummoxed faces that were pulled on the Manchester United bench, as an army in high-visibility jackets stood and watched it all unfold, suggested they took a dim view.

News.title: Brian Madjo, 17, electrifies Villa despite Super Cup defeat by PSG
News.content:
His team played with all the resilience and bravery that has become a trademark, epitomised by the powerful Madjo and another teenager in midfielder George Hemmings.

Emery said: “Brian has scored goals for us in pre-season and has shown his capacity to work in our idea. I am so happy because the young players were involved in our work and not playing last season.

“Of course there is still work to do but they showed they can play with us. They have responded fantastically and will then feel the confidence. With a loss you can never be happy but overall I am proud of all the players and everything we’ve done. Some changes will be needed but we’re confident.”

This was a fine Villa performance to silence the doom merchants who have been fearing a troubled season. After the painful sales of Morgan Rogers, Youri Tielemans and Lucas Digne, Villa are clearly a team in transition. They are operating under restrictions to comply with Uefa’s financial rules and there is still the possibility of another important player leaving before the transfer deadline day.

England centre-back Ezri Konsa remains a priority target for Premier League champions Arsenal, and was absent here. Konsa, Emiliano Martínez and Ollie Watkins were all granted extended leave after their participation in the World Cup, which has done little to ease the fears of supporters over more departures. The trio will return to training this weekend.

While some outsiders are predicting a difficult season for Villa, do not bother telling Emery. He has turned putting noses out of joint into an art form since sweeping into Villa Park and with him around anything feels possible.

The Basque remains optimistic about the future and those hopes will only have been underlined by the performance of Madjo. He bullied PSG centre-back Willian Pacho for much of the evening and even managed to steal the limelight from PSG’s magician Khvicha Kvaratskhelia.

News.title: Advice, cookbooks and emergency pot noodles: Your best gifts for university students
News.content:
When it comes to sending a child or grandchild off to university, it can be tempting to fill their room with every conceivable gadget.

So to help, we asked the Telegraph Recommended Community for their best gift recommendations and their suggestions ranged from desk lamps to cookery books and supermarket gift cards.

Here are the essentials worth buying.

Kitchen basics

From cupboard essentials to electrical appliances and cookbooks, most readers say they’d gift kitchen equipment.

Thinking back to his university days, reader TJ, 43, from London, says “the main essentials are around kitchen items and good long lasting food”.

“It’s nice to have some bits to cook for others as well and to make friends quickly,” he adds.

Susan, 54, from the West Midlands, agrees, recommending “basic cooking equipment” as a key staple and “distinctive cutlery, plates and cups that are easily identified”, which are particularly useful for shared accommodation.

“A box of store cupboard ingredients such as olive oil, soy, stock cubes and spices to use when cooking,” is also well-received, she says.

News.title: Everton dispatch Newcastle to give Matthias Jaissle a reality check
News.content:
Newcastle United manager ​Matthias Jaissle is ‌refusing to dwell on the departure of key players that has left his club in turmoil going into the new season, as they step up their preparations against Everton at Murrayfield this evening.

Jaissle was recruited from Saudi Pro League side Al-Ahli after Eddie Howe left last month, with the German coach joining a club who have lost Anthony Gordon, Sandro Tonali and captain Bruno Guimaraes in quick succession.

“It’s a challenge, a big challenge, always when there’s a transitional period. ‌But it’s ‌not time to ⁠complain, it doesn’t make sense to see the negative things,” Jaissle said.

“We want to see the chance in that situation and that’s our approach from day one. We are here to do our ⁠best job. We want to support the players, the current squad.

“There will be adjustments to see in the coming days, weeks. But for now it’s only focused on the daily work, the work we can influence. That’s all that ​matters now.”

The 38-year-old coach arrived in Newcastle ‌having won two Austrian Bundesliga titles with Red Bull Salzburg before leading Al-Ahli to back-to-back AFC Champions League crowns.

He remained tight-lipped about new signings.

“Obviously, in that transition phase, the players who left the club were ‌great ​players, great characters, experienced ⁠players. This is now a vacuum,” he said.

“Either we adjust something in the squad, by signing these players, these profiles, or other players ⁠need to step up and fill ​these positions, these leadership roles. I’m quite optimistic, we can work in both scenarios.”

Jaissle said he had a ​clear vision of how he wants his team to play.

“The phrase how Newcastle ‌should play like is front-footed, intense, ​aggressive and of course also successful. ​In the end, it’s all about what ⁠I can ⁠say and it’s also why I’m sitting here,” he said.

“The approach we have as a coaching team and the identity of Newcastle is famed for, it’s so linked so close together - which is a perfect fit in my eyes and ​that’s going to be exciting.”

Team news on the way shortly.

News.title: Ebola outbreak ‘doubling every 20 days’, warns UN chief
News.content:
Congo’s runaway Ebola outbreak is doubling in size every 20 days, according to the United Nations humanitarian chief, putting it on track to soon be the largest ever seen.

Three months after the outbreak was officially declared, the case load is expanding exponentially and many believe the true toll is far higher than recorded.

If cases continue to double at the same rate, the flare-up in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) will surpass the record West African outbreak sometime around the end of September.

Modelling by one health analytics firm already predicts there is a more than 90 per cent chance that the DRC will become the largest on record.

The two-year West African outbreak grew to more than 28,600 cases and 11,325 deaths across Sierra Leone, Liberia and Guinea from late 2013 to 2016.

This year’s outbreak centred on the DRC province of Ituri has already seen 4,449 cases and 2,061 deaths in only a few months.

News.title: Madagascar forced to divide and share mpox vaccine as epidemic takes off
News.content:
Authorities in Madagascar are being forced to split single vaccines into fifths to try to protect as many people as possible during an ongoing mpox outbreak.

The method, known as “fractional dosing”, is authorised by the World Health Organization (WHO) in emergencies when there are critical vaccine shortages, but is not routinely recommended and carries a level of risk.

Madagascar, the African island with a population of roughly 33 million people, is currently battling its largest-ever outbreak of the virus formerly known as monkeypox, with at least 4,000 cases recorded so far.

Another one million people are thought to be at risk of contracting clade 1b mpox, a fast-spreading strain of the virus that emerged from the Democratic Republic of the Congo in late 2023.

High risk groups include sex workers, young children, and people living with HIV/Aids. Medical workers are also at risk.

“Public health authorities in Madagascar have been given too few doses to protect the at-risk population; they were initially given 30,000 doses in May, and a subsequent 30,000 have just arrived at the end of July,” said Akhil Bansal, a doctor of internal medicine working on the mpox response in Madagascar and a policy fellow at the Centre for Global Development.

“However, we need to vaccinate more than one million people, so we have been “fractionally dosing”, or splitting vaccines, into fifths, to stretch the supply as far as we can.

“This is a somewhat established approach for vaccines, but even then, the number of doses we have is insufficient,” said Dr Bansal.

Sports.title: Michael Carrick reveals plans for more signings before transfer deadline and target for first season Man Utd as boss
Sports.content:
MICHAEL CARRICK wants two more signings at Manchester United before the transfer window closes.

United are in the market for a left back and a midfielder as they approach the final fortnight of the window.



The club have held informal discussions with Newcastle full back Lewis Hall’s representatives but Newcastle have taken measures to dampen talk of a move.

United are prepared to settle for Arsenal left back Myles Lewis-Skelly as an alternative but consider his asking price to be too high.



United made a fresh enquiry for Real Madrid midfielder Aurelien Tchouameni last month and have monitored Carlos Baleba at Brighton for over a year.

Andrey Santos and Youri Tielemans have come in to bolster the United midfield but Carrick is keen on more incomings.

He Said: “I think we’ve got a pretty good balance in all when you lay the squad out, but yeah, of course, we would like more.

“We would like more, we need to keep pushing for more.

“There are one or two areas where we’d like to improve and we feel that there’s the possibility to improve.

“But again, that needs to be something that we can do that makes us better and improves the group, whether that’s quality or whether that’s a little bit of depth.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

“That’s something we’ve got to manage. That’s pretty obvious.”

Manchester City, Tottenham and Chelsea have all spent at least £100m on a signing and newly-promoted Ipswich Town and Coventry City have outspent United so far this summer.

United invested £85m on Santos and Tielemans, having baulked at the valuation of the £116m Anderson and Mateus Fernandes, who moved to Tottenham for £85m.

Carrick added: “Money’s money. I get that. It’s still about the football and that’s where the competition lies.

“So I think there’s a balance of responsibility of this club to – and what we feel naturally as a group anyway – is to try and win games and be successful.



“We feel like we’ve got to be pushing for everything that we’re involved in, understanding a little bit, being realistic of what the recent history’s looked like as well, and that’s over a period of time.

“But then actually the confidence we’ve taken from the last few months, and what we kind of achieved in the league.

“So there’s a lot that goes into that, but certainly the situation is what it is as well, whether that’s finances or whatever.



“For now, we’ve got to make the most of it, but we’ve got to keep pushing, really, and push everything in every boundary that we can to be able to win again, basically.

“And that’s the challenge at the end of the day, whether that’s this season or hopefully the one after. It needs to be, I say it needs to be, we want it to be as soon as possible, and that’s what we’re all aiming for.”

United are the only club from the old “Big Six” in the Premier League to have not spent £100m on a signing.

When asked whether United can win the title without a £100m player, Carrick replied: “A little bit depends on what position that is and what you’ve got and what dynamics you need at certain points.

“Sometimes you do need that if it’s the right player. Again, it’s not purely on money.



“Just the money doesn’t guarantee you, it needs to be the right player and a better player for what we’ve got.

“It’s something obviously over time we need to, we need to be pushing to look to enhance the squad all the time in different ways.

“So, yeah, 100 per cent we need to do that.



“It’s constant communication of where, what work we need to do, where we want to improve.

“But again, a lot of it’s the dynamics of the group, where we are, personalities.

“Character’s one thing, what we think we can get out of certain players in certain positions, what direction we want to go in.

“But yeah, we’re pretty clear in the messages that we need to keep pushing and there’s certain things that we want to try and do, but it needs to be right as well.”

Sports.title: Arsenal agree deal to sign Liverpool and England youth striker Vincent Joseph, 16, in major academy coup
Sports.content:
ARSENAL are working to complete the signing of wonderkid Vincent Joseph.

The striker, 16, left Liverpool earlier this summer after turning down the chance to sign scholarship terms.



The Gunners have an agreement in place with the teenager over personal terms but must agree a settlement fee with Liverpool.

If the two clubs are unable to come to an agreement then a tribunal will take place to determine what the reds are owed.



The Professional Football Compensation Committee will be tasked with deciding the fee should negotiations bear no fruit.

The PFCC sets a transfer figure for players under the age of 24 who move clubs before signing a professional contract or after the expiration of such a deal.

Multiple factors will be taken into consideration by the PFCC should Arsenal and Liverpool fail to reach an agreement, including Joseph’s age and the time he was at Liverpool.

Joseph would be an impressive signing for Arsenal and he has scored eight goals in nine appearances for England’s Under-16s.

He also bagged three goals in two appearances for Liverpol’s Under-18 Premier League side.

The Gunners are working hard to bolster their academy sides this summer after poor performances in recent years.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

Axel Donczew, the youngest player to ever represent Cardiff, is set to join the club.

Striker Mylo Bernard, who is also 16, is also making his way to the Emirates after turning down the chance to stay with Crystal Palace.

Arsenal have made some changes to the academy this summer and Pascal De Maesschalck is now running the show.

The Belgian replaced Per Mertesacker, who left at the end of last season, and reports into sporting director Andrea Berta.



Recruiting the best young talent around is a key part of Arsenal’s plan to improve their youth sides.

There is a desire to bring in British players, as they can arrive at 16, but the club are looking abroad, too.

And Ecuadorian twins Edwin and Holger Quintero will join next year once 18.

Sports.title: Arsenal ‘make final decision on Martin Zubimendi transfer exit amid Real Madrid interest’
Sports.content:
ARSENAL reportedly have no intention of selling Martin Zubimendi to Real Madrid this summer.

The Euros and World Cup winner, 27, only landed in North London last year and featured in every single Premier League game as Arsenal became champions in his debut season.



Real Madrid tried to beat the Gunners to Zubimendi last summer but there was no going back on the £51million deal Arsenal had struck with Real Sociedad by the time Los Blancos attempted to hijack it.

Real are said to have maintained an interest in Zubimendi one year on.



But according to football.london, Mikel Arteta wants him to be part of his bid to win back-to-back titles.

It is understood that Zubimendi, as with most other Arsenal players, would be attainable for the right price.

But it could take something astronomical to prise him away from the champions, and from a manager who wants him to stay.

Zubimendi’s starting spot could be under threat this season following the £75m signing of Bruno Guimaraes from Newcastle.

Declan Rice is a guaranteed starter in the midfield three when fit, and ousting skipper Martin Odegaard could be a tough ask. Mikel Merino, Eberechi Eze and Max Dowman are also in the mix.

If Arteta gets his wish and Zubimendi sticks around as a rotation option, Myles Lewis-Skelly could, in theory, be pushed closer to the exit door.

Chelsea and Manchester United have both been offered the chance to sign the Hale End academy graduate, who can play at left-back or in midfield.

But with Arteta stacked in both departments, the £60m-rated 19-year-old may soon be on the move.

Blues boss Xabi Alonso wants to cut five centre-backs from his squad this summer.



Trevoh Chalobah has already joined Italian side Como as part of the clearout.

Chelsea are holding out for £25million for Badiashile, who joined from Monaco for £35m in 2023.

Sports.title: Man Utd new-boy Youri Tielemans shares statement APOLOGISING after being accused of ‘offending’ and ‘undermining’ Villa
Sports.content:
MANCHESTER UNITED star Youri Tielemans has apologised to Aston Villa after claiming his new club were “above” them.

The Belgium midfielder, 29, sealed a £35million switch to Old Trafford after the Red Devils paid his release clause.



But Tielemans ruffled a few feathers after admitting United were one of the clubs bigger than Villa.

He said: “I am very thankful to Aston Villa. I owe them the world. It is a great club, we did amazing things, and they have put me back to my best level.



“But there are clubs above Villa, and Manchester United is one of them.”

His words didn’t go down well with some Villa supporters as some asked if the jibe was “necessary”.

And he put out an apology for Villa fans after the “mistake” of his “choice of words”.

He wrote on his Instagram story: “Never meant for my words in the press yesterday to offend anyone or undermine the institution of Aston Villa Football Club, which I massively respect and I’m grateful to for the past 3 years.

“I must however admit my mistake and apologise for my choice of words, will be more careful in the future.

“Wishing the club the best in the future. Youri.”

“At the times that I have been linked with the club before, it did not happen, but it is what it is. I just keep working, keep doing my thing on the pitch and then it happens.

“It is a great achievement for any footballer to end up here. It means you have done well in your career. But it does not end there. I want to be successful.”



Tielemans was a key figure in Villa’s top 2025-26 season that saw them finish fourth and win the Europa League.

He started 21 times for Villa in the Prem last season, assisting four goals.

Tielemans also scored a further two on their path to Europa League glory, assisting three.

Sports.title: Italy ‘to hand shock national team debut to highly-rated teen striker wanted by Brazil’
Sports.content:
ITALY could be set to hand a competitive debut to highly-rated youngster Samuele Inacio to fend off interest from Brazil.

Inacio, 18, is a Borussia Dortmund starlet who is beginning to make waves since making his first-team debut last season.



Born in Bergamo, Italy, to a Brazilian father playing in Serie A at the time, Inacio is eligible to play for either nation.

So far in his career he has chosen the country of his birth, being capped at a number of age groups in Italy’s youth system.



He even made his senior debut earlier this year in a friendly against Luxembourg.

But Brazil scouts are said to be circling, given that the youngster is free to change allegiances until he makes his first competitive appearance for either country.



Gianluca DiMarzio reported that the national team, currently fronted by Carlo Ancelotti, sent scouts to watch Inacio as Dortmund took on Arsenal in a pre-season friendly at the weekend.

They watched him open the scoring against the Premier League champions just seven minutes into the contest, helping his side to an eventual 3-2 win.

The Italian football insider went on to suggest Italy under new manager Roberto Mancini are eager to lock the starlet down before his head can be turned.

They could even cap him at the earliest opportunity, the September international break, to commit his future to Italy, where reports say his loyalties still lie for the time being.

Sports.title: Michael Carrick confirms Man Utd's Marcus Rashford plan as transfer reality becomes clear
Sports.content:
Michael Carrick confirms Man Utd's Marcus Rashford plan as transfer reality becomes clear

Marcus Rashford has returned to Manchester United following loan spells with Aston Villa and Barcelona as Michael Carrick prepares to reintegrate him into the squad

View 2 Images Marcus Rashford is back in the Manchester United picture

Michael Carrick insists Marcus Rashford still has plenty to offer Manchester United this season with it now looking increasingly likely he will stay at Old Trafford.

‌



The England international hasn't played for his boyhood club since December 2024, when he was frozen out by former manager Ruben Amorim. Since then, he has had loan spells with Aston Villa and then spent last season with Barcelona.

‌



It was expected that he would secure a permanent move to the Camp Nou, but their decision to sign Anthony Gordon meant they opted against triggering his £26million clause.

‌



He now returns to United, where he could make his return, ironically, against Amorim's AC Milan this weekend. The Manchester Evening News report both sides believe it is most likely he will remain at his parent club and Carrick is confident he will be a positive presence in his squad.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

"He's a very good player, and I think if you're going to have a career over 10 or 15 years, there's going to be times when things go in a direction and maybe a different direction," he said.

‌



"I think there are ups and downs, and that doesn't judge you as a one-off kind of judgment. It's what happens over time, and now we're in a positive place as a group, and Marcus can offer us so much. He has done, and he can do again, so in that respect, it's quite exciting."

Had Amorim stayed in charge, it is inconceivable that the burnt bridges would have been able to be mended, but Carrick has a history with Rashford and has helped to smooth the process.

And while Carrick stopped short of definitively confirming he will stay at United, he described him as 'our player' and said he is being treated the same as anyone else within his squad.

‌



View 2 Images Rashford has not played for Manchester United since December 2024 (Image: Getty Images)

"He's our player, he came back Sunday night, he arrived with Kobbie [Mainoo], and Lisandro [Martinez] came the day after, and he's part of the group like anybody else. He came in, he's trained really well.

"I've known him a long time, like I've known some of the others a long time, so I don't treat him any different to anybody else, but it's been good to have him around the group again this week. So I'm really positive with that."

‌



Carrick added that he was confident the returning Rashford would bring something new to his options and help balance the squad for the upcoming Premier League campaign.

He added: "We're really calm, we just treat it like anybody else coming into the group and there's obviously this slight twist that he knows the club as well as anybody and that's a real positive.

‌



"He's been here all his career, all his life before the last 18 months or so, to understand what it means. That side of things is natural, that's a given. I know he's got history, but I've got history with a number of the players as well, so that doesn't make that a unique situation at all and treat him as exactly like any other player.

"Bringing him into the group and carrying on as normal brings the good things that we haven't got, and we want to get that balance with every individual player, and Marcus has come back and he's in good form, and it's been good to have him around this week."

Sports.title: Michael Carrick tells Man Utd owners exactly what he needs in rest of transfer window
Sports.content:
Michael Carrick tells Man Utd owners exactly what he needs in rest of transfer window

Manchester United have gone a month without announcing a transfer in the summer window and manager Michael Carrick has urged the hierarchy to get deals over the line

View 2 Images Michael Carrick is keen for new players at Manchester United (Image: Ash Donelon/Manchester United via Getty Images)

Michael Carrick has sent a clear message to the Manchester United hierarchy by telling them to "keep pushing" for more transfers this summer.

‌



United have signed Youri Tielemans and Andrey Santos, from Aston Villa and Chelsea respectively, to strengthen their midfield, while Karl Darlow arrived from Leeds on a free transfer to become the back-up goalkeeper. But their total expenditure of £85million lags way behind their Premier League rivals.

‌



It has now been a month since United announced a new signing and, with just 19 days left until the transfer deadline on September 1 and nine until United's first game of the 2026/27 season, Carrick has made his feelings clear.

‌



"I think we've got a pretty good balance in all when you lay the squad out, but we would like more, we need to keep pushing for more," he told the Manchester Evening News.

‌



"There's one or two areas where we'd like to improve and we feel that there's the possibility to improve, but again, that needs to be something that we can do that makes us better and improves the group, whether that's quality or whether that's a little bit of depth. That's something we've got to manage. That's pretty obvious."

Carrick wants to sign a left-back to compete with Luke Shaw, with Newcastle's Lewis Hall the top target, as well as another central midfielder. His squad only had to compete in the Premier League following his arrival as interim boss in January to replace Ruben Amorim and Carrick knows the upcoming campaign will be more demanding, with United back in the Champions League and cup competitions.

This summer has seen huge transfer fees become even more normalised, with Morgan Rogers, Elliot Anderson and Sandro Tonali all moving for £100m or more. Remarkably, United's record transfer remains the £89m they paid Juventus for Paul Pogba in 2016.

‌



View 2 Images Andrey Santos has impressed Michael Carrick since his £50m transfer (Image: Michael Campanella/Getty Images)

Asked if United may need to break that record this summer, Carrick said: "A little bit depends on what position that is and what you've got and what dynamics you need at certain points. Sometimes you do need that if it's the right player.

"Again, it's not purely on money, the money doesn't guarantee you, it needs to be the right player and a better player for what we've got. It's something [that] over time we need to be pushing to look to enhance the squad all the time in different ways."

‌



Carrick has been delighted by the impact that Santos, in particular, has made since joining for £50m from Chelsea. And he stressed that communication with director of football Jason Wilcox and chief executive Omar Berrada remains good.

"It's constant communication of where, what work we need to do, where we want to improve," he said. "We're pretty clear in the messages that we need to keep pushing and there's certain things that we want to try and do, but it needs to be right as well."

Sports.title: Anthony Taylor calls out ex-officials in the media for creating 'culture of fear' for refs
Sports.content:
Anthony Taylor calls out ex-officials in the media for creating 'culture of fear' for refs

Anthony Taylor has just called time on his spell as a Premier League referee and he has bemoaned the fear culture, which former officials contribute to

View 2 Images Anthony Taylor has called time on 16 years of Premier League refereeing

Anthony Taylor admits the presence of ex-referees in the media criticising their decisions does lead to "a culture of fear, disrespect and shame."

‌



The former Premier League official has called time on his career, retiring last month after appearing at a second World Cup. He officiated 668 matches in the English game, which included every major domestic cup final as well as 163 international fixtures.

‌



Taylor and Michael Oliver have been among the leading names in the refereeing game for years, but that meant the spotlight on them was increased and their decisions were heavily analysed.

‌



A number of former referees, the likes of Keith Hackett, now have columns with media outlets and are free to cast their opinion on referees and the decisions they make - which Taylor admits had a detrimental impact on the environment officials had to work in.

Quizzed by the BBC on whether that type of commentary bothers him Taylor concedes: "Yes, it does personally, because it doesn't have any balance to it a lot of the time.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



"It's just part of the focus that comes with football. When we're dealing with supposedly objective analysis of matches, whether that be an expert ex-player in a studio or an ex-referee, that should be balanced and fair. If it's all one-sided criticism, that creates a culture of fear, disrespect, shame.

"There's a thirst for people to be told: 'Is the decision right or wrong?' And the reality in football is there's a lot of subjectivity and opinion in the middle of right and wrong. But that's not acceptable a lot of the time now."

During his career Taylor had to deal with questions over his conduct with the official making a high-profile error in a game between Burnley and Swansea, which came just days after his stag do in 2017. Taylor would admit it was a "terrible" call, but the timing of his trip was irrelevant.

‌



View 2 Images Anthony Taylor admits the commentary from former officials is not helpful

Taylor, who will now take up a role leading referees in Turkey, admits that officials are only human and the outside noise certainly impacts on them.

"Any referee will be lying to you if they said that pressure or that scrutiny did not bother them," he said, "because that's a natural human reaction. One of the challenges that referees face at every level is actually understanding the challenges that we face.

Article continues below

"Fear of making mistakes, external opinion, spectators, managers, parents, media, colleagues. All these things feed into creating self-doubt, lacking confidence, and then things can spiral out of control and you lose the ability to actually have any confidence in what you're doing on the field."

Sports.title: Man Utd star Youri Tielemans issues grovelling apology over comments in interview
Sports.content:
Man Utd star Youri Tielemans issues grovelling apology over comments in interview

Manchester United summer arrival Youri Tielemans has been forced to apologise after his comments following the cross Premier League move

View 2 Images Youri Tielemans joined Man United in the summer. (Image: Manchester United via Getty Images)

Manchester United midfielder Youri Tielemans has been forced to apologise following his comments after leaving Aston Villa. The summer arrival claimed that the Red Devils were above his former employers, whom he helped back to European silverware with their Europa League triumph.

‌



The Red Devils made the move for the 29-year-old during the summer as they triggered the £35million release clause within his contract. Tielemans ended his three year spell in the West Midlands and arrived as part of the reinforcements in Michael Carrick's midfield, a problem position at Old Trafford in recent years.

‌



However, Tielemans sparked anger with his comments in his first extended sit-down with journalists as the conclusion to United's pre-season preparations looms closer.

‌



Wayne Rooney lands new Man Utd gig alongside Mark Goldbridge for Gary Neville's Overlap READ MORE :

Michael Carrick provides Marcus Rashford transfer update with telling Man Utd statement READ MORE :

In a post to Instagram, he said: "Never meant for my words in the press yesterday to offend anyone or undermine the institution of Aston Villa Football Club which I massively respect and I'm grateful to for the past three years.

"I must however admit my mistake and apologise for my choice of words, (I) will be more careful in the future. Wishing the club the best in the future. Youri."

Factions of the Villa Park faithful appear to have taken umbrage with the comments made by the Belgium captain. Tielemans said: "I am very thankful to Aston Villa. I owe them the world.

‌

"It is a great club, we did amazing things, and they have put me back to my best level. But there are clubs above Villa, and Manchester United is one of them.

"It is a great achievement for any footballer to end up here. It means you have done well in your career. But it does not end there. I want to be successful."

‌



Tielemans has featured prominently during the preparations for the new season, which begin on August 22 with a trip to newly promoted Hull City.

View 2 Images Andrey Santos and Youri Tielemans have joined United this summer (Image: Ash Donelon/Manchester United via Getty Images)

United's final game of their pre-season build-up comes against AC Milan, managed by Ruben Amorim who was sacked by the Red Devils in January.

‌



United have been busy in the window, acquiring Andrey Santos to help bolster their midfield, while work remains ongoing to further strengthen positions across the pitch.

It is an important season for Carrick and his side as they return to the Champions League following last season's third-place finish. All eyes will be on whether they can compete on all fronts, however, on the pitch the focus will be on alleviating the burden on Bruno Fernandes.

The United captain has been instrumental for the club during a dour period in the club's history. Tielemans has already talked up the relationship with his midfield partner.

He said: "It's really natural. He is a guy that can find space easily. I just try and find him so that he can move forward."

Sports.title: Steven Gerrard's call to Virgil van Dijk that saw Liverpool win Man City transfer battle
Sports.content:
Steven Gerrard's call to Virgil van Dijk that saw Liverpool win Man City transfer battle

Virgil van Dijk was the subject of a transfer tug-of-war involving Liverpool and Manchester City with a phone call from Steven Gerrard proving key

View 2 Images Liverpool signed Virgil van Dijk despite interest from Man City

Steven Gerrard has recalled a phone call he received from Virgil van Dijk when he was being pursued by Liverpool and Manchester City where he delivered a blunt message to the defender.

‌



Van Dijk had established himself as one of the Premier League's best centre-halves and made it known to Southampton that he wanted to move on. A summer move failed to materialise, but the saga was always going to continue come January.

‌



Liverpool would win the race, spending a then club-record £75million to land Van Dijk, who made an instant impact as he helped the Reds make the Champions League final within months of joining.

‌



Gerrard recalls Van Dijk phoning him to so that he could get a greater impression of the Merseyside outfit. The Dutchman wasn't looking for the Liverpool legend to sell him the club, instead seeking a greater insight, but Gerrard did make it clear that Liverpool's traditions far exceeded City's.

The former midfielder recalled during Captains, a new LFC Original: “He phoned me at the time actually. I knew his agent really well. It was City, Liverpool.

“He said to me, ‘I haven’t phoned you to sort of push me one way or the other, because I know which way you’re going to push me. But just tell me a little bit about Liverpool?’

‌



“I just said to him, ‘Look, if it’s about what the clubs stand for and what the clubs are about, you’re wasting your time because I think you already know the answer to that.’ It was an interesting conversation and I was so happy that he chose us.”

View 2 Images Virgil van Dijk scored on debut for Liverpool back in 2018 (Image: Getty Images)

Van Dijk would enjoy the dream debut, scoring against Everton to knock them out of the FA Cup and concedes he was determined to wear red. “That feeling of, like, I wanted to play for this club so badly, it was so intense," he said. "And the fans embraced me from day one. Scoring also against Everton [on his debut] helped massively too!”

Article continues below

Within 18 months of signing Van Dijk had been named the PFA Player of the Year and proved crucial in Liverpool's Champions League success of 2019. The following year he helped the Reds' end their 30-year wait for a top flight title. Van Dijk remains Liverpool's defensive leader despite turning 35 this summer.

Sports.title: Liverpool 'pull out of transfer deal' for attacker after holding talks with agent
Sports.content:
Liverpool 'pull out of transfer deal' for attacker after holding talks with agent

Liverpool are pushing to bring in a winger before the window shuts on September 1 and had earmarked Bradley Barcola's PSG team‑mate Ibrahim Mbaye as a possible option

View 2 Images Liverpool have stepped away from pursuing a deal for Ibrahim Mbaye (Image: Getty Images)

Liverpool have cooled their interest in Ibrahim Mbaye after discovering that a combined deal for him and Bradley Barcola could approach €200m (£171m). With the summer window ticking down, Liverpool are intent on signing at least one more winger.

Mbaye, capable of operating on either flank, became PSG's youngest-ever starter at just 16-years-and six months, but his route to regular minutes remains blocked by Ousmane Dembele, Khvicha Kvaratskhelia, Desire Doue and Barcola. Liverpool's initial interest followed Mo Salah's departure earlier in the summer and continued uncertainty around Cody Gakpo ’s future.

However, Fabrizio Romano reports that Liverpool have now stepped away from a potential move after holding talks with Mbaye's agent. Via his YouTube channel, it is claimed that Liverpool held talks with super agent Jorge Mendes over Mbaye, but PSG quoted the Reds around €200m for the pair.

Liverpool could end up signing two new wingers for Andoni Iraola's squad, especially if Cody Gakpo joins Tottenham, but they believe that PSG's asking price for Mbaye is currently too high. Reports indicate PSG value Mbaye between €40m (£34m) and €50m (£42m).

Liverpool news: Andoni Iraola set to be handed new transfer priority as double update emerges READ MORE :

FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Liverpool have already added one wide option this summer, bringing in Osasuna's Victor Munoz for £34m, but with Munoz operating on the left, the club still need a natural right‑sided winger to fill the long‑standing role previously held by Salah. Barcola, who was left out of Wednesday's UEFA Super Cup final against Aston Villa, remains an option as uncertainty over his future continues.

PSG president Nasser bin Ghanim Al‑Khelaifi has also declined to rule out a potential departure, telling beIN SPORTS after the match: "We’re working calmly, we don’t talk too much, we do.

"I can’t say whether he will leave or not. Today, he is a PSG player. We’ll see!"

PSG boss Enrique sidestepped a question on Barcola's future, adding: "I don't know and I don't want to speak about any player individually because it's always dangerous when you are asking something positive or negative about a player. I stay focused on my team."

View 2 Images It remains to be seen whether Liverpool will meet PSG's asking price for Bradley Barcola (Image: Adam Davy/PA Wire)

Liverpool's chase has hit a major stumbling block, with PSG valuing the 23‑year‑old at around £145m - a fee that would eclipse the £125m Liverpool paid for Alexander Isak last summer. Romano adds that talks between the two clubs are still ongoing, with Barcola himself keen on making the move to Anfield.

With the window entering its final stretch, it remains unclear whether the Reds side will go anywhere near that price. Iraola made his need for a winger clear from the very start of pre‑season. "There are obvious situations where we need to sign players," he said.

"Winger for example, we definitely need to sign a winger, but there are other situations where we will have to analyse what the market gives you, what is the cost, how we also see the players we have."

So far Iraola has welcomed Jeremy Jacquet and Ronald Araujo as well as Munoz.

Sports.title: Celtic sign midfielder Baur on an initial four-year deal
Sports.content:
Celtic have made their fourth summer signing with midfielder Mika Baur joining on an initial four-year deal, with the option for a further year.

The 22-year-old arrives in a deal worth around £6.8m, joining from German club Paderborn, after helping them win promotion from the second tier of German football to the Bundesliga.

He scored four times and provided five assists across 33 league appearances last season, and was named the club's player of the year.

Sky Sports News understand the Scottish champions will pay an initial fee of around £4.5m for Baur, with £2.3m in add-ons making up the deal.

Similar to deals struck with fellow summer signings Camilo Duran, Kasper Høgh and Haissem Hassan, a large proportion of the bonuses will be paid out if Celtic reach the league phase of the Champions League.

"I've had a good pre-season with good matches and tough training sessions, everything. So I'm in good shape and I'm ready to go."

Sports.title: Richards to face Kalajdzic showdown on Fisher bill
Sports.content:
British former world title challenger Craig Richards will take on Radivoje Kalajdzic in a 10-round light heavyweight showdown, while Lee Cutler faces Louis Greene in a middleweight clash, on Zuffa Boxing's Johnny Fisher bill at London's Copper Box Arena.

Richards vs Kalajdzic will serve as the chief support bout to the 10-round heavyweight main event featuring Fisher at Zuffa Boxing 11 on September 26, live on Sky Sports.

An opponent for 'The Romford Bull' will be announced in the coming days.
