“LaLiga, in ​coordination with both clubs and the RFEF, agreed to postpone the match between Celta and CA Osasuna scheduled ⁠for next Sunday at Abanca Balaidos due ​to ​a problem affecting ​the stadium’s turf, which is ​currently unfit ‌for football,” ​the ​league said in a statement.

Sports.title: Arsenal had ‘disgraceful’ offer for Premier League star instantly rejected as transfer decision looms
Sports.content:
Arsenal have expressed interest in signing Ezri Konsa, but their initial offer fell way below his true valuation.

That's the view of Gabby Agbonlahor, who outlined how much Aston Villa will want for the defender this summer.



3 Konsa sits top of the centre-back wishlist at Arsenal Credit: Getty

Konsa is understood to be the leading centre-back target for Premier League holders Arsenal amid injuries in the position.

William Saliba is out for an 'extended period' with a back issue that he picked up at the World Cup, whilst Jurrien Timber is still recovering from a groin injury.

It leaves Gabriel, Piero Hincapie and Cristhian Mosquera as their only options, though left-back Riccardo Calafiori can play at centre-back if needed.



Arsenal have made Konsa a target after his impressive performances for England at the World Cup, but appear to be far away from a deal.

How much did Arsenal offer for Konsa?

talkSPORT's Ben Jacobs gave an update on the potential move during Breakfast and confirmed that the Gunners are real suitors for Konsa.



"I'm keen to know what Gabby thinks because Villa have already been desecrated. There's no release clause as per Lucas Digne (£6million to Paris Saint-Germain and Youri Tielemans (£35m to Manchester United).

"But Arsenal are serious, despite links with Cristian Romero. He's off to Atletico Madrid, €40million (£34m).



"And Arsenal have actually already made a verbal offer, but this was a few weeks back and there was a huge gulf in valuation. My information is that Arsenal's valuation was in and around £35million..."

"Pardon?" a shocked Agbonlahor interjected before Jacobs continued: "And Aston Villa are looking for £60million, £65million and maybe, in this inflated market, even more...

"But ultimately, if you think about Arsenal, they'll be looking at some other defenders that have gone maybe outside the Premier League.

3 Agbonlahor could not believe that Arsenal had valued Konsa so low Credit: talkSPORT



"If you look at the Villa perspective - one, they don't want to sell, two, Jan Paul van Hecke (Brighton to Tottenham Hotspur), £52million, Maxence Lacroix (Crystal Palace to Chelsea), £52million.

"Ezri Konsa, England international, should ultimately be more, so it's just whether Arsenal are prepared to, effectively in their eyes, overpay.

"Whereas, Villa would say £60million, £65million. In this market, that's still decent value for money."

Agbonlahor then offered a Villa perspective as he explained: "I get it though, Ben, because he's got two years left.



"I've said it many times, his performances in the World Cup, his performances since his first day at Aston Villa... he'll be looking at (Marc) Guehi next to him, 'What's he earning at Manchester City?'

"Aston Villa can't get to those levels of £250k-a-week, maybe £300k-a-week, whatever he's earning, Guehi. He deserves that money.

3 Arsenal want to sign a new centre-back before the window shuts on September 1 Credit: Getty

"But Aston Villa will also say, 'Listen, we can't give you that money, but we need at least £65million, £70million'. £35million is a disgrace of an offer. If he had a year left, I'd get it, but not with two years left."



Jacobs then said: "By the way, when they made that offer, that was the perspective of Aston Villa. It was dismissed out of hand.

"So Arsenal are now coming back off the back of those talks, off the back of that gulf in valuation, and they have to decide whether they're going to significantly improve their offer

"And if they do, I think there's a fair chance it might happen. Jacobo Ramon at Como is another possibility, but Arsenal want to add a centre-back between now and the end of the window."

Konsa has made 286 appearances for Villa across all competitions and won the Europa League with them last season.



Formerly of Charlton Athletic and Brentford, a move to Arsenal would see him return to his birthplace of London.

Sports.title: How Manchester United are expected to line up for first 2026/27 Premier League match
Sports.content:
How Manchester United are expected to line up for first 2026/27 Premier League match

Michael Carrick will be forced to deal with an injury crisis heading into his first season as permanent Manchester United manager.

The Red Devils boss was promoted from his caretaker role in May after guiding the club back into the Champions League.

5 Carrick must juggle an injury crisis heading into the new season Credit: Getty

United finished third in the Premier League last term having lost just two of his 17 matches in charge.

His side will begin the new season away to newly-promoted Hull City on the opening weekend.

The two clubs meet at the MKM Stadium on Saturday, August 22 at 12.30pm, live on talkSPORT.

However, how will United line-up under Carrick when they take on the Tigers?

United injuries

The former midfielder will be without some key players heading into the first weekend of the season.

Several of those have been absent throughout pre-season, though, giving Carrick a chance to prepare for how he will cope until their return.

Matthijs de Ligt remains sidelined until September with a long-term back injury.

Meanwhile, Manuel Ugarte is set to miss the majority of the season after undergoing surgery on a knee injury suffered at the World Cup.

Kobbie Mainoo and Lisandro Martinez have both been unavailable so far this summer, with the latter forced off in the World Cup final with a thigh injury.

Benjamin Sesko also remains a doubt to face Hull due to the shin injury he suffered in May.

5 Sesko is one of eight players who could miss United's clash with Hull Credit: Getty

The Slovenia striker has yet to feature for United so far in pre-season ahead of their final outing against AC Milan on Saturday.

Mason Mount could miss out too after he was forced off against Paris Saint-Germain earlier this month.

Goalkeeping duo Karl Darlow and Tom Heaton are also currently absent, with the former still recovering from minor surgery.

How will United line-up on opening day?

Carrick has used his favoured 4-2-3-1 formation throughout United's pre-season schedule.

The shape was his preferred system as the Red Devils rallied to finish in the top four last term.

Fortunately for him, first-choice stopper Senne Lammens is fit after featuring for Belgium at the World Cup.

5 Summer signing Youri Tielemans is set to feature in midfield for United Credit: Shutterstock Editorial

The full-back positions are also at a full compliment, with Diogo Dalot and Luke Shaw likely to start the season on the right and left, respectively.

With Martinez and De Ligt both absent through injury, Carrick's centre-back options have taken a hit.

Whilst Ayden Heaven did impress when called upon last season, Harry Maguire and Leny Yoro are likely to get the nod against Hull.

Moving into midfield, summer signings Andrey Santos and Youri Tielemans have both featured heavily this summer.

The departure of Casemiro, paired with Mainoo and Ugarte's injury, means they are set to form a new-look pairing in the centre of the park.

In front of them, captain Bruno Fernandes remains United's creator-in-chief when it comes to the four-man attack.

5 Bruno Fernandes remains United's key man after a stellar season last term Credit: Getty

Amad Diallo has solidified his starting role on the right in pre-season, but there is more of a debate to be had on the left wing.

Full-back Patrick Dorgu has been converted into a wide forward under Carrick with three goals and one assist since his arrival.

Meanwhile, Marcus Rashford re-joined the squad ahead of Wednesday's friendly against Leeds United following his loan spell with Barcelona.

Despite that, Matheus Cunha can be expected to begin the season on the left flank for United.

As a result, Bryan Mbeumo will fill the void left by Sesko's enforced absence at centre-forward.

The 27-year-old, who did not go to the World Cup after Cameroon failed to qualify, scored 11 league goals during his first season with United.

Sports.title: UEFA ready to force Gianni Infantino exit and introduce rotating FIFA presidents
Sports.content:
Senior European football figures met in Salzburg ahead of the UEFA Super Cup to discuss the FIFA crisis, talkSPORT understands.

This included a meeting between UEFA president Alexander Ceferin and European Football Clubs chair Nasser Al-Khelaifi.

4 Al-Khelaifi has been Paris Saint-Germain's president since October 2011 Credit: Getty

The pair were pictured alongside each other as Al-Khelaifi's Paris Saint-Germain beat Aston Villa 2-1. And perhaps more significantly, Confederation of African Football president Patrice Motsepe was also in attendance.

talkSPORT understands constructive talks took place with Ceferin stressing the need for a change of leadership and governance within FIFA, including discussions at a pre-match lunch at Red Bull’s famed Hangar-7 museum.

Talks have been described by multiple sources as positive with UEFA intent on holding Infantino to account for the failure of FIFA Forward Enterprise, and accepting nothing less than his immediate resignation or the withdrawal of his candidacy ahead of March’s election.

talkSPORT understands Ceferin is even prepared to spearhead a vote of no confidence, that requires backing from 43 members to trigger an emergency vote, if Infantino continues to fight on.

It is viewed by many as a logical next step, and a more practical one than a boycott.

Which candidate is UEFA likely to back as Infantino's replacement?

UEFA are also prepared to back other candidates to stand against Infantino with CONCACAF president Victor Montagliani and Asian Football Confederation president Sheikh Salman bin Ibrahim Al Khalifa potential options.

As of now, UEFA has not collectively recommend or supported any one candidate.

Al-Khelaifi would also be a popular choice as FIFA president, but said after PSG's win he's 'very happy' as PSG president.

Although Gianni Infantino has firm backing in Africa, and a few Asian federations on side, FIFA could essentially come to a gridlock without UEFA support. A boycott of FIFA competitions, potentially starting with the Under-20 Women's World Cup in Poland, is just one option UEFA are considering.

Refusing to engage with key FIFA meetings and even breaking away via a joint UEFA, CONCACAF and AFC venture are all under discussion.

4 Ceferin and Al-Khelaifi had plenty to discuss during the Super Cup Credit: Getty

The EFC is also a key player in all this as the body represents over 850 European clubs.

The EFC is a firm ally of UEFA, both generally and on the topic of how FIFA should be governed going forward.

Several insiders argue that any governance shake-up of FIFA should include a greater voice for clubs in global football matters. One topic to watch is whether the ‘E’ (European) in EFC turns to ‘W’ (worldwide) one day.

Another sub-plot is whether federations in Africa will remain universally in favour of Infantino. It was significant that Motsepe was also at the Super Cup.

Multiple sources have told talkSPORT his attendance was in part to discuss Infantino's future rather than solely to support African referee Omar Artan, who officiated the game after being banned from entering the USA to referee at the 2026 World Cup.

Speaking to Sky, Motsepe urged FIFA’s members to let the election decide Infantino’s fate, but stopped short of directly backing the under-pressure FIFA President.

4 Infantino's relationship with US President Donald Trump has proved extremely controversial Credit: Getty

"If you want to take him out, go for elections,” he said. “Let the 211 member associations decide. Do that and the vote will express whether they've got confidence in him or not."

Although no one has publicly come forward yet to run against Infantino, the November 18 deadline is currently viewed as secondary to a potentially more imminent vote of no confidence that could be triggered before it. Ceferin’s hope is that Infantino walks before this is necessary.

talkSPORT understands UEFA not only want Infantino gone, but to also rethink the FIFA presidency itself.

How could a new-look FIFA presidency operate?

This could see rotating presidents to dilute the office’s power, or even removing the title altogether and replacing it with a chair.

This could also see a series of vice-chairs providing further checks and balances, and a governance model not too dissimilar to the civil service.

Whereas Infantino pushed to align FIFA's commercial, operational and regulatory arms under one partly-privatised subsidiary, senior UEFA figures prefer a clear separation in each of these areas.

4 Infantino has, to date, refused to show any signs of quitting his post Credit: Getty

FIFA were approached for comment and pointed towards 'constructive and positive' talks in Morocco from select members of FIFA's leadership.

FIFA sources also reiterated their statement from last week which pointed to the fact, “The FIFA president was democratically elected by FIFA member associations and continues to serve with their mandate.

"Those who do not have the support of FIFA member associations should not seek to achieve through allegation, insinuation or misinformation what they cannot achieve through FIFA's established democratic processes.”

Sports.title: ‘Pardon?’ – Gabby Agbonlahor stunned as Premier League star branded ‘future Ballon d’Or winner’
Sports.content:
Gabby Agbonlahor was left bemused by a caller who claimed Arsenal star Myles Lewis-Skelly is a future Ballon d'Or winner.

Lewis-Skelly was a first-team regular for the Gunners in the 2024/25 season, establishing himself as first-choice left-back for Mikel Arteta's men.

3 Myles Lewis-Skelly - Future Ballon d'Or winner? Credit: Getty

However, the youngster lost his starting spot to Riccardo Calafiori last season, while Piero Hincapie made more league starts on the left side of defence than the 19-year-old as Arsenal ended a 22-year wait to win the Premier League.

The England international ultimately played a key role as the Gunners pipped Manchester City to top spot, impressing in midfield in the final weeks.

Even so, Lewis-Skelly has been linked with a summer exit following the arrival of Bruno Guimaraes from Newcastle.

talkSPORT understands that the player has been offered out to a number of Premier League clubs this summer.

One caller, though, can't understand why Arsenal would be willing to let Lewis-Skelly leave, even branding the teenager a future Ballon d'Or winner.

"I can't see why Arsenal would wanna let go, in my opinion, a future Ballon d'Or winner," the caller, Kieran, said on Breakfast on Wednesday.

"Pardon!?" was Agbonlahor's immediate response.

"I think he'll be a future Ballon d'Or winner," Kieran replied.

To which Gabby, again, replied: "Pardon!?"

The Lewis-Skelly aficionado elaborated: "I can't see a player at 19 years old, in the centre of midfield, that conducts the game the way he does!

3 Agbonlahor was having none of the Lewis-Skelly Ballon d'Or shouts Credit: talkSPORT

"In the big games, he's clutch! We cannot afford to let him go."

At that point, Kieran lost signal, which the returning Alan Brazil picked up on: "Oh! Sorry Kieran! We've lost you there."

Agbonlahor continued: "Talking that much nonsense, his phone network's said: 'Alright, that'll do you mate!"

Arteta address MLS speculation

Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta was asked about Lewis-Skelly's future following their pre-season friendly win over Italian outfit Como in the week.

Lewis-Skelly's celebration during the penalty shoot-out win heightened rumours he could leave the Emirates this summer.

Arteta, though, refused to draw on speculation surrounding the Arsenal star, stating: "He’s a very emotional player. Remember when he did all the gestures on the pitch. I am not going to talk about any speculation.

3 Arteta addressed speculation linking Lewis-Skelly with a summer exit Credit: Getty

"If there is any speculation about our players it is a good sign, it means we attract attention and they are doing a good job."

Lewis-Skelly may yet start Arsenal's Community Shield clash with Manchester City on Sunday 16 August.

The Gunners face City in the Premier League curtain-raiser in Cardiff this weekend.

Sports.title: Evan Ferguson in line for another European loan 20 months after last Brighton appearance
Sports.content:
Evan Ferguson in line for another European loan 20 months after last Brighton appearance

Italian side Genoa are interested in signing striker Evan Ferguson on loan, talkSPORT understands.

Ferguson, who hasn't played for Brighton since December 2024, spent last season on loan with Serie A powerhouse Roma.



2 Ferguson started just 10 league matches for Roma last season Credit: Getty

However, he was restricted to just 16 league starts owing to an ankle injury he sustained in March.

The switch to the Olimpico came after a disappointing stint at West Ham for the second half of the 2024/25 season.

Even so, Genoa are keen to bring the Republic of Ireland international back to Italy for a brief spell.



This comes despite Ferguson's extended spell on the sidelines owing to the aforementioned ankle issue.

The 21-year-old is absent until October at the earliest, meaning a permanent departure is unlikely.



'We'll see the best of him'

Former Newcastle and Aston Villa goalkeeper, and compatriot, Shay Given believes that Ferguson would benefit from a loan move to Celtic.

Ferguson has previously been linked with a move to the 2025/26 Scottish Premiership champions, though has never played for Celtic.



"If you have a manager like Martin O’Neill at Celtic who can trust Ferguson, put him in, and put his arm around his shoulder, I think we will see the best of him," Given said.

"Martin is brilliant at that with his man management. The Celtic fans would be very excited to see Evan arrive in Glasgow too.

2 Ferguson would benefit from a move to long-term admirers Celtic, claims Shay Given Credit: Getty

"I just think he needs to go somewhere where the manager is a bit old school about these things.



"Someone who will tell Evan you are my number nine, you are going to play every week, you are my main man. I’m putting a lot of eggs in your basket, I believe in you, so don’t let me down.

"I don’t think it’s about sports science or tactics. He needs to go to a club where he can settle, feel that confidence again, and put the injuries behind him and go on a good run."

On Ferguson's fitness issues, Given added: "The last couple of seasons must have been so frustrating for him.

"After every injury he has had to go back and nearly start with another miniature preseason again, five or six times a season. It is not ideal.



"Would a move to Celtic be a make or break moment for Evan Ferguson? No, because Evan doesn’t strike me as the sort of character where you can break him like that.

"The only thing that can break him at the minute is his injury record."

Ferguson has previously been touted to take the Premier League by storm.

However, the Irish forward has failed to kick on following his hat-trick against Newcastle in 2023 that announced the striker to the world.

Sports.title: Youri Tielemans issues apology to Aston Villa fans after poor ‘choice of words’
Sports.content:
Youri Tielemans issues apology to Aston Villa fans after poor ‘choice of words’

Youri Tielemans admitted it was a 'mistake' to publicly claim there were clubs 'above' Aston Villa, including Manchester United.

The newly-acquired Red Devil made the controversial comment during a roundtable interview with several reporters.



2 Tielemans is expected to play a starring role in United's midfield Credit: Getty

"I am very thankful to Aston Villa," Tielemans said.

"I owe them the world. It is a great club, we did amazing things, and they have put me back to my best level.

"But there are clubs above Villa, and Manchester United is one of them. It is a great achievement for any footballer to end up here. It means you have done well in your career. But it does not end there. I want to be successful."

Tielemans' comments evidently did not go down well with sections of Villa's fanbase, prompting him to issue an apology on social media.



Youri Tielemans' apology to Aston Villa fans

"Never meant for my words in the press yesterday to offend anyone or undermine the institution of Aston Villa Football Club which I massively respect and I'm grateful to for the past three years," Tielemans wrote.

"I must however admit my mistake and apologise for my choice of words, will be more careful in the future.



"Wishing the club the best in the future. Youri."

Tielemans made the move from Villa to United in July after the Red Devils triggered his £35million release clause.

Youri Tielemans' Aston Villa career at a glance

It brought the curtain down on Tielemans' three-year stint at Villa Park, having joined on a free transfer in July 2023 following his departure from Leicester City.



While at Villa, Tielemans helped the club qualify for the Champions League twice and reach the FA Cup semi-finals.

2 Tielemans has joined his third different English club Credit: Getty

But his most iconic moment in a Villa shirt came during last season's Europa League final.

Tielemans opened the scoring with a remarkable first-time volley, slamming home Morgan Rogers' floated cross from the left.



The 29-year-old's goal proved to be the first of three on the night for Villa as the Europa League triumph ended their 30-year trophy drought.

Tielemans then linked up with Belgium following the end of the club season and helped his nation reach the World Cup quarter-finals, where they were beaten by Spain.

Sadly for Tielemans, he did not play a part in Belgium's loss against Spain having picked up an injury during the warm-up.

Prior to Belgium's quarter-final exit, Tielemans had played all but five minutes of the nation's World Cup campaign.

Sports.title: West Ham will be weaker than two Championship rivals unless they make double signing
Sports.content:
West Ham will be weaker than two Championship rivals unless they make double signing

talkSPORT host Jeff Stelling has predicted West Ham will not achieve automatic promotion unless they sign Troy Parrott and Jamie Vardy.

Many pundits are tipping the Hammers to steal an immediate return to the Premier League at the first time of asking.

4 Keeping hold of Bowen has set the Hammers up for a Championship title tilt Credit: Getty

The Irons managed to retain their key forward Jarrod Bowen and kicked off their competitive campaign with a 3-1 victory over Portsmouth in the Carabao Cup.

Bowen registered the joint-fifth most goal involvements in the top-flight last term, scoring nine goals and providing nine assists.

History is on West Ham's side: the last time the club competed in the second tier back in 2011/12, they secured an immediate return to the top-flight via a 2-1 playoff final victory over Blackpool at Wembley.

This season, the Opta supercomputer lists West Ham as favourites for both the title (17.2%) and automatic promotion (29.4%).

Hammers push for attackers

However, that is not the view of talkSPORT's Stelling, who tipped Middlesborough to win the league and said: "I think Wolves might go up automatically too. I think they might need to spend again.

"I've got a lot of experience in Kieran Trippier and Raúl Jiménez, and you saw Raúl Jiménez at the World Cup; he looks well capable of scoring goals in the Championship.

"West Ham I've got in the playoffs; I think they've lost too many and not enough incoming. So I've got them in the playoff.

4 Hull have been promoted to the Premier League via the playoff route last season Credit: Getty

"But I tell you what, if they sign Troy Parrott and Jamie Vardy, then I'll flip that round with Wolves. But that's an if at the moment."

talkSPORT understands the Irons are making a strong push to sign Parrott from Dutch side AZ Alkmaar, after the Republic of Ireland international scored an impressive 51 goals across the last two seasons

The ex-Tottenham youngster's £18million price tag could prove a bargain if he orchestrates a successful promotion charge.

The Hammers submitted an initial £15million bid for the ex-Tottenham youngster which was rejected by the two-time Eredivisie champions, but an improved offer is expected ahead of their Championship opener against Burnley.

Concerns persist at the London stadium regarding attacking depth, with Pablo still waiting to score his first goal for the team following his £21million arrival from Gil Vicente in January.

While Taty Castellanos has been a goalscoring threat since arriving from Lazio in January, the departure of Callum Wilson to Brentford leaves the unproven Pablo as the only other senior option upfront.

4 Parrott was handed his senior Spurs debut by Mourinho Credit: AFP

4 Vardy has experience of being promoted to the Premier League twice Credit: Getty

The Hammers have received over £137million from the sales of Crysencio Summerville to Al-Hilal and Mateus Fernandes to Spurs.

By contrast, Nuno Espirito Santo's side have only spent £6.2m on incoming talent, including Keiber Lamadrid and Manor Solomon.

However, one potential arrival would not cost a transfer fee. Vardy is a free agent after leaving Italian side Cremonese following their relegation from Serie A

talkSPORT understands the 39-year-old is assessing all options, with a number of clubs enquiring over his availability.

Wolves target Premier League return

Meanwhile, Wolves are also targeting automatic promotion as they kick off their league campaign on Friday against Blackburn Rovers - live on talkSPORT.

The Molineux outfit take their place in the Championship for the first time since 2017/18, following a disastrous Premier League campaign in which they finished bottom with just 20 points.

Wolves enter the season with a new manager in the dugout, with Rob Edwards sacked and replaced by Portuguese Cesar Peixoto, who led Gil Vicente to a shock sixth-place finish in the Primeira Liga in 2025-26.

They have also secured the return of Raul Jimenez, after the Mexican striker spent three seasons at Fulham, netting 28 Premier League goals in that time.

Heading into the campaign, Opta's supercomputer have given Wolves a 19.2 per cent chance of automatic promotion back to the top flight.

Sports.title: Southampton set for vicious Championship abuse as Tonda Eckert decision ripped apart
Sports.content:
Southampton set for vicious Championship abuse as Tonda Eckert decision ripped apart

Tonda Eckert is incredibly lucky to still be the manager of Southampton - but he can expect a vitriolic campaign.

The south coast side were dragged through the mire at the end of the 2025/26 season having been caught spying on Championship play-off semi-final opponents Middlesbrough.

2 Saints intern Will Salt was caught filming Middlesbrough's training session before their play-off first leg in May

Saints won the two-legged affair 2-1 on aggregate having played out a 0-0 draw at the Riverside in the first leg.

However, Eckert's side were booted out of the play-offs in the wake of 'Spygate' after it was confirmed that Saints broke the rules.

The intern caught spying, Will Salt, was also offered a permanent position at the club.

Eckert was also hit with three three FA charges after a scandal that dominated football for weeks.

The German boss, though, kept his job at the St. Mary's helm despite sullying the club's name.

Championship opponents have been quick to highlight when they'll be playing Southampton in the 2026/27 season, which gets underway Friday night.

And Clarke believes that Saints will come in for some hostile receptions in the coming campaign.

'They're going to get hammered'

Speaking on the talkSPORT Daily podcast, EFL expert Adrian Clarke said: "I was staggered that Southampton stuck with Tonda Eckert. He did bring the club into disrepute; it was a serious offence or offences.

"And, let's be honest, these are just the incidents that they've admitted to.

"I find it odd that there's just those three and that that wasn't maybe something they did more often.

2 Eckert remains in charge at St. Mary's after he was publicly backed by the club's owner Credit: PA

"But anyway, it's just, yeah, I personally would have moved on from that manager and tried to just bring in somebody fresh because the hangover is not going to be pretty.

"They're going to be the boo boys, Southampton. Everywhere they go in the Championship this season, they're going to get hammered by opposition fans.

"They're going to be calling them cheats. They're going to be the team everybody loves to hate.

"And that might inspire them, but it also might not be that pleasant for anyone involved at Southampton. So I just think, yes, he's a good manager. Yes, he's a good coach. But there are other good coaches out there.

"He's darkened the name of your football club. And I would have got rid.

"The only reason, the only reason Tonda Eckert is still manager of Southampton is because he's good. If the chairman thought, 'I'm not sure about him,' he would have sacked him straight away. Trust me."

When are Southampton's key fixtures?

Saints kick off their Championship campaign with a trip to Watford on Sunday 16 August - live on talkSPORT 2.

They then play their first home game the following week when they host Stoke.

Eckert's men face rivals Portsmouth in mid-October, one of 10 Championship games that'll be free to watch on ITV.

And they face Middlesbrough for the first time since the 'Spygate' punishment was handed out in late November.

Sports.title: Ruben Amorim wields the axe at AC Milan: Former Man United boss tells EIGHT stars they have no future at the club - including Chelsea flop - as he implements his five-at-the-back system
Sports.content:
Ruben Amorim has told seven AC Milan stars that they have no future with the Italian giants as he implements a brutal cull in his first summer at the club.

Former Chelsea stars Fikayo Tomori and Christopher Nkunku are among the octet being driven out of Milan by the ex-Manchester United boss.

Amorim took charge at the San Siro in early June, just over six months after he was sacked by the Red Devils, where he won 38.1 per cent of his games.

He has got off to a poor start in charge of the Rossoneri, drawing against Celtic and Inter Milan and losing 3-0 against Chelsea last Saturday.

But the Portuguese will have the chance to put things right against his old employers in two days' time as Milan face United in Wroclaw, Poland.

Alongside Tomori and Nkunku, he has put up for sale Youssouf Fofana, David Odogu, Pervis Estupinan, Santiago Gimenez and Philip Terracciano.

Ruben Amorim has told seven AC Milan players they no longer have a future at the club

Former Chelsea flop Christopher Nkunku will be shown the door, Daily Mail Sport understands

Tomori has had interest from Coventry City, managed by his old gaffer Frank Lampard, while Crystal Palace, Nottingham Forest, and Villarreal are looking into Fofana.

Amorim held a crunch meeting with club bosses on Thursday to discuss his plans for the season, which inevitably involve instituting his five-at-the-back system which flopped so hard at Old Trafford.

He has accepted the task of transforming Milan's fortunes after they finished fifth last season in Serie A, which only qualified them for the Europa League.

Another of his tasks will be to sort out the future of winger Rafael Leao, who has been linked with the likes of Galatasaray and Leeds. He has been actively looking for a club.

Amorim is ready to embrace the challenge, and suggested that his task at the San Siro is even greater than his job at Old Trafford.

'I'm really very happy to be here, it's an honour to be the coach of Milan,' he said.

'Why did I choose Milan? If you read an old interview of mine you will understand it, for me a special club.

'It's a very big challenge that I accepted even if after the last one [at Manchester United] I told myself to accept a smaller one.

'Perhaps it is a greater challenge than the last. I'm proud to be here, we all are, me and my staff.

Fikayo Tomori is another of the eight stars who Amorim hopes will be saying arrivederci

'I'm at Milan to win, if you're Milan coach you have to have this mentality,' he added.

'I'm not naive, I know there's a lot of work to do, but if you're the Milan coach you have to play to win.'

Milan last won the Serie A title in 2021-22 under Stefano Pioli.

Last campaign they were managed by Massimiliano Allegri, who had been successful with them and Juventus previously but struggled to replicate those heights despite them having no European football.

Sports.title: 'If Henry Pollock wants to get involved, that offer is open': How new 'Ultimate Sevens' wants to shake up rugby - thanks to England's rising star, Sunderland's owners and the Hundred
Sports.content:
Henry Pollock wants to have a crack at playing sevens at the Los Angeles Olympics in 2028. Transferring to the sport's shorter format will not be easy – especially in the wake of Matchroom Talent Agency head honcho Eddie Hearn’s demands for Pollock to be paid as much as a million pounds a year by his club employers Northampton Saints. But it is not impossible. There are options out there.

‘Should Henry want to get involved and do a bit of sevens preparation this year or next, that offer remains open,’ Barney Pascall, the managing director of a new sevens tournament aiming to shake up the rugby market, tells Daily Mail Sport.

‘It’s a great story that high-profile players in the sport want to play sevens. If Eddie wants to call, I’ll be ready.’

Pascall is the man heading up Ultimate Sevens, which will begin next month after investing ‘tens of millions’ in a competition which will take place in Madrid, Cardiff, Biarritz and London across four consecutive September weeks.

Rugby’s conservative ecosystem has been ripe for a new arrival for some time. R360, the proposed 15-a-side rebel league, failed to get off the ground amid rejection from the game’s existing authorities. But Ultimate Sevens wants to work alongside them, having spotted what Pascall sees as a gap in the market.

‘This is about elevating rugby sevens,’ he says. ‘We've been incredibly focused on being complementary to the ecosystem and there's a reason for that. It's because we can be.’

Henry Pollock’s representative Eddie Hearn has made it clear English rugby’s new sensation wants to have a crack at playing sevens at the Los Angeles Olympics in 2028

‘This is about elevating rugby sevens,’ says Ultimate Sevens founder Barney Pascall. ‘We've been incredibly focused on being complementary to the ecosystem. There's a reason for that'

2026 ULTIMATE SEVENS FIXTURES Sep 5 – Ontime Butarque Stadium, Madrid Sep 12 – Cardiff Arms Park, Cardiff Sep 18 – Parc des Sports Aguilera, Biarritz Sep 24 – Gtech Community Stadium, London

The funding needed to create Ultimate Sevens has not been insignificant. Its backers are BIA Sports Group (BSG), whose portfolio also includes Premier League side Sunderland.

It is aiming to capitalise on the growing popularity of rugby sevens, which has gone to a new level since France 15-a-side superstar Antoine Dupont won gold at the 2024 Paris Games, and also attract a new audience who may not be familiar with the sport at all.

Interestingly, in doing so, Ultimate Sevens has adopted a marketing slogan of ‘don’t call it rugby’ in a move similar to the one the England & Wales Cricket Board made when it created The Hundred. Like The Hundred, Ultimate Sevens has created new teams. Like The Hundred – which remains unpopular with cricket traditionalists – it wants to broaden rugby's appeal. It also plans to one day follow in the cricket competition’s footsteps by selling its sides to private investment.

‘It was an opportunity for us to be a bit punchy and challenge existing perceptions of rugby,’ Pascall says of his competition's commercial outlook. ‘It was a bit playful too. People who know sevens call it exactly that. If you're not in the rugby ecosystem, I think the slogan asks the question: “Well, if it's not rugby, what is it then?” That creates a hook and a level of interest.

‘I find it a compliment to even be in the same breath as The Hundred because they have tried and I think succeeded in bringing new audiences to cricket. We’re absolutely clear we want the integrity of the sport to remain at the heart of what we're doing. Sevens is a very credible sport. It’s existed since 1883. We want to add to that.’

Like The Hundred, Ultimate Sevens' six teams have both men’s and women’s outfits. The newly created sides are Albion Athletic, Atlantic Novas, Clan Taran, Foudre Bleue, Pacific Current and Sol Feroz. In time, Pascall wants to attract rugby’s biggest names such as Pollock. But season one will see the teams dominated by experienced sevens players.

Each of the four tournaments will see the men’s and women’s sides from the six teams play in a straight knockout format. All the action will be completed in one day, which is different to the traditional World Series Sevens circuit whose competing teams are nations. Matches will be ten minutes long with teams given the option of a 90-second tactical timeout.

One new innovation is around conversions. Tries scored under the posts will be worth an automatic seven points. If a try is scored wider out, teams can opt to take their additional kick from different, more challenging positions in a bid to earn more points. The range available is one, two or four points depending on the kick’s difficulty. Tickets for the London event at Brentford’s Gtech Community Stadium start at £30.

Rugby sevens' popularity has gone to a new level since France 15-a-side superstar Antoine Dupont won gold at the 2024 Paris Games

Like The Hundred, Ultimate Sevens has created new teams. Like The Hundred, it is open to selling its sides to private investment

‘The kicking rule adds another layer of entertainment and sporting jeopardy,’ says Pascall, who is assisted in the new competition’s creation by former England sevens captain Tom Mitchell as sport and innovation director. ‘This isn’t about a one-season wonder. This is a long-term play. This is about being around for many years to come. Younger and female audiences are increasingly introduced to rugby through sevens. That’s a powerful tool.’

For too long, rugby has badly needed investment as, outside the international 15-a-side game, it continues to experience financial difficulties. Fresh financing into PREM Rugby has been welcomed and so too should BIA’s arrival. Rugby as a whole will benefit if Ultimate Sevens can become a regular part of its landscape.

‘People ask me what success will look like,’ Pascall says. ‘I want people, in time, to know these players. That’s more of a qualitative than quantitative outcome, but if we get to that point, I think we'll have done something really special.

‘I absolutely believe this investment in the sport is going to be a positive energy for rugby, for Great Britain’s Olympic hopes, and for other countries around the world.’

Sports.title: Enzo Fernandez is the face of the ugly game and Enzo Maresca should run a mile from him. Replacing Pep Guardiola at Man City is already the hardest job in football without once again indulging Argentine's graceless, brainless behaviour
Sports.content:
It is not a surprise that Manchester City appear to be pursuing Chelsea's Enzo Fernandez, a player who has come to symbolise much that is ugly about the beautiful game.

City's new manager, Enzo Maresca, has got form for indulging and rewarding the graceless and base antics of the Argentina midfielder that goes back to his time in charge at Stamford Bridge.

Two years ago, Maresca was forced to defend his decision to select Fernandez as Chelsea captain in their opening game of the 2024-25 season, against City, just a month after Fernandez posted a video of him and other Argentina players mocking the racial heritage of the France team.

Chelsea team-mate Wesley Fofana branded the video, uploaded by Fernandez after Argentina's victory over Colombia in that summer's Copa America final, as 'uninhibited racism'. Fernandez apologised. And in the absence of Reece James, Maresca made him skipper.

What Fernandez did was brainless as well as offensive. This is a player, don't forget, who was suspended by his own club at the end of last season after he flirted publicly with Real Madrid. This is a player who helped to get Liam Rosenior the sack at Chelsea when his performances dipped noticeably.

This is a man who is up there with the worst in the league in his attempts to pressure referees with his antics. This is a player who was sent off in the World Cup final and whose thuggish, unpunished behaviour in the semi-final against England prompted widespread disgust.

It is not a surprise that Manchester City appear to be pursuing Chelsea's Enzo Fernandez, who in the last couple of years has come to symbolise much that is ugly about the beautiful game

City's new manager Enzo Maresca has got form for indulging the graceless and base antics of the Argentina midfielder that goes back to his time in charge at Stamford Bridge

In those circumstances, and given Chelsea set an asking price of £120million, it was predictable that Madrid did not want to go anywhere near him. It was less predictable that they would take the unusual step of stating publicly they were not interested in buying him.

'The club wishes to state,' read the Madrid communique at the beginning of July, 'that it has not made any efforts, either directly or indirectly, aimed at signing the aforementioned player and, furthermore, has no intention of pursuing such an operation.'

But now, a couple of months into the job, Maresca is already risking the reputation City built in their Pep Guardiola years, for being a side that was widely admired for the quality, style and attitude with which it went about dominating the Premier League.

Chelsea have set a deadline of 5pm on Friday for City to make a bid for Fernandez and meet their asking price but it is possible the story will bleed further towards the transfer deadline of September 1.

City under Guardiola were the team of gifted stars like Kevin De Bruyne and Bernardo Silva. They were the team of Rodri and Ilkay Gundogan, Jack Grealish and Erling Haaland. They were a team that put a smile on the face of any neutral that watched them.

The purchase of Fernandez, if it happens, will change that. Fernandez is a fine player but his quality comes at a high cost in terms of the image of the team he plays for. The wisest managers buy character as well as quality.

The truth is that if City buy Fernandez, it will represent not just a downgrade on Rodri but a reversal of much that the club stood for under Guardiola. It will represent an embrace of the ugly side of the game. It will be a transfer that stands for cynicism. It will be a move that says City are swapping beauty for the game's dark arts.

The truth is also that Chelsea overpaid for Fernandez when they agreed to give Benfica £106.8million for him in the aftermath of the 2022 World Cup. He has not been as big a failure as some of the BlueCo signings but he has mixed some outstanding performances with periods of near anonymity.

The truth is that if City buy Fernandez (right), it will represent not just a downgrade on Rodri (left) but a reversal of much that the club stood for under Pep Guardiola

It will represent an embrace of the ugly side of the game. It will be a transfer that stands for cynicism. It will be a move that says City are swapping beauty for the game's dark arts

He is supposed to be one of the leaders of the team but there were spells last season when he looked nothing like a leader. Leaders don't flirt with other teams. Leaders don't get suspended by their own club. Leaders don't allow mediocrity to flourish all around them.

Chelsea finished tenth in the Premier League last season, 33 points adrift of champions Arsenal and Fernandez was part of that surrender. If Chelsea do sell him to City and somehow manage to recoup the money they paid for him, it should be cause for a huge celebration on the King's Road.

There are early signs, in fact, that Chelsea, under their own new manager Xabi Alonso, are starting to pursue a more coherent transfer policy and achieve a better balance in their playing staff. If Fernandez leaves, it will be another step in the right direction.

For City, it would be the opposite. Maresca already has the most difficult job in English football in attempting to replace Guardiola. If he signs Fernandez, that job will get a whole lot harder.

Sports.title: 'We can achieve something really special': Man United boss Michael Carrick on aims for new season, the future of Marcus Rashford and why Andrey Santos is a 'dream'
Sports.content:
Michael Carrick strides in to a plush conference room here at Carton House, the five-star spa hotel which has been home to Manchester United all week, with a big smile on his face. There's a lot for the United boss to be happy about, after all.

Back home his daughter, Louise, has collected her A-Level results and, here in Ireland, the late returns of Kobbie Mainoo, Marcus Rashford and Lisandro Martinez from the World Cup have added a fresh dynamism to a group who overcame Leeds on penalties at Croke Park only a few hours earlier.

Carrick, unlike predecessor Ruben Amorim, is level-headed. When the tough questions come his way, bosses are relaxed that Carrick won’t rock the boat like Amorim, who United face on Saturday in Poland when they play AC Milan, would do.

It’s why United were comfortable throwing open the doors to Amazon filmmakers for this season’s ‘All or Nothing’ behind-the-scenes documentary.

But don't mistake his calmness for ambivalence. Carrick is determined to win, too.

This has been a summer where top four rivals Chelsea, Manchester City and Tottenham have all spent north of £100million. Even newly-promoted Coventry and Ipswich have spent more than Manchester United. His message here, though, was crystal clear to those upstairs.

Man United boss Michael Carrick spoke to reporters on the club's pre-season trip to Ireland

United overcame Leeds on penalties at Croke Park in a friendly on Wednesday evening

'It can't be for the sake of it, but yeah, of course, we want to improve, we need to improve,’ Carrick says. ‘It's something that we're working towards, for sure.’

So far only Youri Tielemans, Andrey Santos and back-up goalkeeper Karl Darlow have arrived to strengthen the first-team squad. Tynan Thompson, an £8m pick-up from Tottenham, is seen as one for the future.

‘I have to say, Karl, Andrey, and Youri, are exactly what we hoped, exactly what we expected in every way,’ he adds.

‘Andrey, for such a young man to come in the way he's come in, his character, his personality is a dream. Literally, he’s a dream.’

But Carrick knows he needs more. United still need a left back - there have been two failed approaches for Newcastle United’s Lewis Hall this summer - and another central midfielder remains on the agenda.

By the time this conversation draws to a close, Carrick had referenced a need to ‘push’ in the transfer market four times.

'I think we've got a pretty good balance in all when you lay the squad out, but of course we would like more,’ he continued. ‘We would like more, we need to keep pushing for more.

‘There's one or two areas where we'd like to improve and we feel that there's the possibility to improve, but again, that needs to be something that we can do that makes us better and improves the group, whether that's quality or whether that's a little bit of depth. That's something we've got to manage. That's pretty obvious.’

Director of football Jason Wilcox is here in Ireland and remains in ‘constant communication’ with Carrick.

With a frugal approach to the summer so far, one which has so far seen them fail to land top target Elliot Anderson, Morgan Rogers, and others, can Manchester United seriously contend for a Premier League title this season?

‘I think you've got to have the belief, you've got to be going into the season thinking we can achieve something special,’ he says, reluctant to commit to any bold proclamation for the season ahead.

‘Don't be going into a season thinking this could be a struggle. We've got to set out to really achieve something.

‘We've definitely got the potential to achieve something really special. I'm not hiding from the fact, and we should aim to do that.

‘I'm not going to make any crazy predictions, but I think on the back of what we've done, I keep saying it, I think that gives us the confidence to move forward. How quickly we keep moving forward, that's the challenge.’

Carrick has been impressed with United's three summer signings so far, particularly Andrey Santos, but he wants more players to come through the door

Carrick was also full of praise for Marcus Rashford, who returned to the club on Sunday

There remains a question mark over Marcus Rashford and the prospect of his first minutes in a Manchester United shirt since 2024, when Amorim left him out in the cold, this weekend.

United have long been open to moving the £325,000-a-week attacker on as part of a plan to reduce the wage bill. They have also been in the market for a left winger all summer, with Crysencio Summerville among the targets, before he opted to move to Saudi Arabia.

Barcelona passed up on their buy option to sign Rashford, who is now back and training well.

‘He's a very good player, Marcus, and I think if you're going to have a career over 10 or 15 years, there's going to be times when things go in maybe a different direction,’ Carrick adds, before electing not to go as far as ruling out a potential move before the deadline.

‘I think there's ups and downs, and that doesn't judge you as a one-off kind of judgment. It's what happens over time, and now we're in a positive place as a group, and Marcus can offer us so much.

‘He has done (in the past), and he can do again, so in that respect, it's quite exciting.’

There’s a return for Kobbie Mainoo too. Carrick kept in touch with Mainoo all summer via text, checking in as he went through the entire World Cup without playing a minute.

There’s no concerns though. In fact, Carrick believes the Mainoo that has come back is ready to take the Premier League by storm.

'The biggest thing for me, Kobbie's in a really good place,’ he adds. ‘I think he feels that. He’s come back and he's come home and he's ready for a big season.’

But there are lingering concerns over squad depth with United competing back in Europe this season.

‘We're not naive, we know what we're going into,’ he concludes, pressed on the fact that United are facing the prospect of 15-20 more games than last season’s historically low total of 40.

‘But we feel we're a stronger group now than we were last season as well in many ways, so we've just got to capitalise on that.’

Sports.title: Paul Pogba's wife hits back at claims he should retire, with 33-year-old set to have Monaco contract ripped up after yet another cruel injury blow
Sports.content:
Paul Pogba's wife hits back at claims he should retire, with 33-year-old set to have Monaco contract ripped up after yet another cruel injury blow

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Paul Pogba's wife has hit back after claims that her husband should retire from football, with Monaco set to rip up his contract.

The former World Cup winner and ex-Man United midfielder has been dogged by injuries in pre-season and multiple reports in France state that his agents are in talks with the club over a mutual termination, at Monaco's request.

Pogba had been trying to revive his career following a doping ban but only featured in six games last season while earning £44,000-a-week at the Ligue 1 side.

He suffered a knee issue after 45 minutes of pre-season and another nasty setback with a thigh injury last week. But with some fans suggesting his body can no longer tolerate playing at the top level, his wife Zulay, 33, defended her husband online.

She wrote: 'For all the people saying Paul should retire or he came back to football for the money, let me make this clear, the only one who knows when he will retire is God.

'And for the ones who say he came back for the money, trust me we are very good with money, thank God.

Paul Pogba's wife, Zulay (right), defended her husband aft

'Social media accepts everything. People can sit behind a screen and say whatever they want, insult someone, question their intentions and forget that there is an actual human being on the other side.

'For those questioning what he has left to prove, let me remind you he achieved the dream every footballer in the world grows up chasing, dreaming to have. He won the World Cup for his country.'

Zulay is a Bolivian model and influencer and the couple met in 2017 before getting married two years later. They have two sons aged seven and six together.

Pogba only returned to training last week after injuring himself in the first game of pre-season but sustained a thigh issue in a small-sided game and was scheduled for an MRI this week.

Daily Mail Sport understands he was offered to MLS clubs in America on Tuesday.

Pogba was allowed back into football in March 2025 after his doping ban was reduced on appeal.

He had already left Juventus after having that contract terminated by mutual consent in December 2024.

Pogba was emotional when he signed for Monaco last summer, describing his comeback as a second chance after what he called 'a time of darkness'.

The midfielder told Daily Mail Sport in 2024 that he discovered news of his reduced ban while preparing for a film premiere, adding: 'We went through hell. A time of darkness. But this is my second chance, I have to use it.'

Sports.title: Man City REJECT fresh Rodri bid from Barcelona with team-mate set for £52m sale to Saudi after Chelsea gave deadline to sign £120m Enzo Fernandez: WINDOW WATCH
Sports.content:
It's that time of the year again – the transfer window is now open until September 1 and it's sure to be a busy period with clubs looking to make big signings ahead of next season.

Here are today's latest developments from Simon Jones and the Daily Mail Sport team...

City reject fresh Rodri bid

Manchester City and Barcelona continue to discuss a fee for midfielder Rodri.

City have dismissed Barca’s latest offer of around £55m as they hold out for closer to £68m for the Spain captain.

Meanwhile, City forward Jeremy Doku has signed a new contract at the Etihad that will keep him at the club until 2031, with an option for a further year.

The Belgium international said : ‘This club means so much to me – I have developed as both a player and a person. I feel settled here, and I know I am improving every day because of the work the staff here do.

‘It’s hard to explain just how much this Club does to help players. I don’t take it for granted and it makes me better.

‘With Enzo here now I am really excited about the new season. His style of football is the kind we love, so that’s exciting for the players.

‘The City fans are also a huge reason I have signed this new contract. I feel their love and support, and it means the world to me. I want to focus of bringing them the success they deserve.’

Barcelona have had a fresh £55million bid for Rodri rejected by Manchester City

Galatasaray move for Martinelli

Galatasaray have made their move for Arsenal winger Gabriel Martinelli with a £38million offer.

However, the Brazilian is not inclined to leave for Turkey.

The 25-year-old is one of the players Arsenal are prepared to listen to offers for with a valuation around £50m.

Roma have also shown interest and it is understood Martinelli will only consider options from the strongest leagues.

Arsenal are re-evaluating options to strengthen their left hand side, they are also continuing discussions with Aston Villa for centre back Ezri Konsa with their latest proposal understood to be around £40m for the centre back.

Al Qadsiah make offer for Reijnders

Saudi Pro League side Al Qadsiah have made an offer of around £52million for Manchester City midfielder Tijjani Reijnders.

Nottingham Forest remain in the frame for the Netherlands international but he is weighing up whether to accept the offer to link up with coach Brendan Rodgers.

Al Qadsiah have been looking to make room for Reijnders arrival.

They are in the process of selling Jeffrey Afriyie to Genk with other departures planned.

It became clear during the pre-season tour of Asia that the 28-year-old was the most likely midfielder to move on before the transfer window closes.

City hold an interest in Enzo Fernandez but Chelsea have imposed a deadline of 5pm on Friday to present a suitable offer for the Argentina international.

It’s understood that City are operating a one-in, one-out system with transfers this month and the exit of Reijnders would free up a space in the engine room.

JACK GAUGHAN

Tijjani Reijnders missed City open training after Al Qadsiah have made an offer for him

Besiktas in the frame for £18m Willock

Besiktas remain in the frame for Newcastle United midfielder Joe Willock.

The 26-year-old has one year left on contract and is valued around £18m. Premier League sides have also shown interest while Besiktas had an offer rejected early this month.

Race for Nwaneri heats up

Interest is building in Arsenal winger Ethan Nwaneri who is considering his options and whether to depart this window.

A number of clubs, including RB Leipzig and other Premier League sides, have been looking to take the 19-year-old on loan or potentially a permanent basis after his disappointing spell with Marseille last season.

Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta praised the England U21 international after his return to pre-season training, saying: ‘Ethan has been really good, probably what happened on the field on his loan in Marseille wasn’t what was expected, and there was a lot of noise and change around the club.

‘But he looks different, a lot more mature, it’s incredible what six months and a different experience abroad can do to you - to be abroad on your own, to go through tough times and to witness that is a part of football you have to be good enough to cope with. I’m very happy with what Ethan has done in pre-season.’

Nwaneri joined Arsenal's academy aged eight and made his Premier League debut against Brentford in September 2022, becoming the youngest player to appear in the English top flight, at 15 years and 181 days old.

He has made 34 appearances for Arsenal and though only made nine appearances at Marseille, still managed to score two goals.

Pape Sarr a target for Al Ahli

Tottenham midfielder Pape Matar Sarr is emerging as a target for Al Ahli in the Saudi Pro League.

The 23-year-old will be allowed to leave if suitable offers arrive and has been the subject of interest from Brentford and Aston Villa as well as other European sides.

Spurs beat off strong competition to sign Sarr from Metz in 2021 and, while he has shown glimpses of what he is capable of, the Senegal international has been inconsistent overall, as have the majority of the squad in recent seasons.

The arrival of Mateus Fernandes and Sandro Tonali mean his starting opportunities will be limited and he is open to exploring a move away.

Spurs are looking to wrap up the sales of Cristian Romero to Atletico and Djed Spence to Inter today.

They remain keen on Manchester City’s Savinho and Cody Gakpo of Liverpool. City’s Omar Marmoush is also on their list.

Villa expected to reject Arsenal offer for Konsa

Aston Villa were expected to turn down Arsenal’s initial proposal of £40million for Ezri Konsa, who is thought to be open to the move.

Villa are also looking to close deals for midfielder Joao Palhinha and left-back Matteo Ruggeri.

TOM COLLOMOSSE

Ezri Konsa is said to be open to a move to the Premier League champions Arsenal

United youngster Williams joins Peterborough

Manchester United winger Ethan Williams has joined Peterborough United for a ‘sizeable’ undisclosed fee.

The 20-year-old, who was part of United’s pre-season tour of Finland, Norway and Sweden, has signed a long-term deal.

Williams had spent time on loan at League Two Cheltenham Town and Scottish Premiership outfit Falkirk.

He said: ‘I have enjoyed my time at [Manchester] United and it's always tough to leave a place like that, but there comes a time in your career where you have to make tough decisions to develop yourself and Peterborough is renowned for helping younger players.’

United’s deal also includes add-ons, a 50percent sell-on clause, a buy-back option and matching rights.

Tigers making moves in the market

Leeds United forward Joe Gelhardt has completed his medical at Hull City ahead of his £4.5million move.

He has agreed a four year contract with option for a further year. Wrexham and Rangers had also made efforts to sign the 24-year-old.

Meanwhile, Hull have formalised their interest in Everton midfielder Tim Iroegbunam with an offer understood to be in excess of £15million.

The 23-year-old has a year left on contract.

If it ain't So?

Brazilian side Palmeiras have signed Fabio So from Burnley.

The 18-year-old made 15 appearances in the U18 Premier League for Burnley, as well as a couple of appearances for the U21s. He left on a free transfer and has signed a contract until the end of January. The contract includes the possibility of an automatic renewal.

Portuguese midfielder So joined Burnley after being at Newcastle's academy.

Amorim's Milan exodus

AC Milan coach Ruben Amorim has decided Fikayo Tomori and Christopher Nkunku do not figure in his plans this season.

The former Chelsea players are available for sale along with midfielder Youssouf Fofana.

David Odogu, Pervis Estupinan, Santiago Gimenez and Philip Terracciano are also expected to leave.

Fikayo Tomori is one of eight AC Milan players who have been put up for sale by Ruben Amorim

Ge-Evan-noa

Brighton striker Evan Ferguson is a target for Genoa.

The Republic of Ireland international was on loan in Serie A at Roma last season, where he scored five goals in 22 appearances, and rivals Genoa would like him to return.

The 21-year-old has been hindered by niggling injuries and damaged his ankle in March but he is also attracting Premier League interest.

Reds youngsters on the move

Liverpool left-back Calum Scanlon is closing on a loan to Cardiff City.

The 21-year-old spent the second half of last season on loan at Cardiff and they have been working hard to bring him back.

Scanlon has impressed on Liverpool's pre-season and attracted a number of enquiries.

League One Sheffield Wednesday, notably, made concerted effort to take the England U20 international to Hillsborough.

Liverpool midfielder James McConnell is a loan target for Championship side Preston North End.

A number of other Championship teams have enquired for the 21-year-old plus League One Leicester City.

Meanwhile, Arsenal are closing in agreement for 16-year-old striker Vincent Joseph who had decided to leave Liverpool last month.

Liverpool offered the teenager a scholarship but he declined and talks are ongoing over compensation.

Sports.title: Real Madrid star Vinicius Jr shows off the results of his cosmetic chin surgery on return to football
Sports.content:
Real Madrid star Vinicius Jr shows off the results of his cosmetic chin surgery on return to football

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Vinicius Jr played his first game for Real Madrid this pre-season, in what was also his first outing since undergoing chin harmonisation surgery.

Real won 1-0 at LaLiga counterparts Deportivo La Coruna, thanks to a first-half stoppage-time goal from Brahim Diaz.

Vinicius Jr started the match before being replaced on 71 minutes for Jorge Cestero by new boss Jose Mourinho.

And while he sported a new look, the Brazilian still could enjoy the winning feeling as they won the Teresa Herrera Trophy.

The winger's facial operation came just weeks after Brazil's last-16 World Cup exit by Norway.

According to Brazilian news outlet TMC, he headed straight to a dermatologist in Goiania when he landed back in his homeland following a short vacation in Europe with on-and-off girlfriend Virginia Fonseca.

Vinicius Jr played for Real Madrid for the first time since having chin harmonisation surgery

His return ended in success as Real beat Deportivo La Coruna to win the Teresa Herrera Trophy

A number of photos of the 26-year-old appearing unrecognisable after the op have gone viral on social media, with fans blown away by his remarkable transformation.

Vinicius Jr posed alongside Dr Alessandro Alarcao, who performed the surgery in Goiania, in another picture that emerged online.

He underwent the procedure, which 'uses fillers to sculpt the facial contour', to add more definition to his chin after being cruelly mocked over it during the World Cup.

It's been an eventful summer so far for Vinicius who was linked with a move away from the Spanish giants – with Arsenal a leading potential destination as he had 12 months left on his contract.

However, any notion about a move to the Premier League ended earlier this month when he signed a new six-year contract at Real until 2032.

Vinicius posted on Instagram: 'Eight years at the Bernabeu are too short.... Six more years, and then forever.'

The club said in a statement: 'Vinicius Jr has become one of the most important players in one of the most successful periods in our history.'

Vinicius Jr joined Real from Brazilian side Flamengo in 2018 and signed a contract extension three years ago.

The Brazil superstar looks completely different after undergoing chin harmonization surgery

🚨 Vini Jr at the clinic after his chin harmonization surgery. pic.twitter.com/WOq8OC0fgs — Madrid Zone (@theMadridZone) July 20, 2026

Vinicius jr is the first person in history to look like the AI version of himself 😭😭 pic.twitter.com/Sqhnd3M0bX — Anabella💙❤️ (@AnabellaMarvy) July 21, 2026

He and Brazil were dumped out of the World Cup at the last-16 stage after a 2-1 loss to Norway

He returned to the club last week for his first pre-season training session and medical assessment following his World Cup campaign with Brazil.

The prolific forward has scored 128 goals in 375 appearances for Real across all competitions, winning two Champions League titles, three La Ligas and a Copa del Rey.

Sports.title: The rivalry of Britain's glam sprinting golden girls - who ignore each other on the track: Amy Hunt goes for European Championships gold quadruple but Dina Asher-Smith stands in her way
Sports.content:
There has already been a British sprinting one-two at this week's European Championships and another could be on the cards as Amy Hunt and Dina Asher-Smith do battle in tonight's women's 200m showpiece.

Newly crowned 100m queen Hunt, 24, is targeting her second gold of the week in her bid for a remarkable quadruple of golds.

Standing in her way is Asher-Smith, 30, who completed the continental sprint double herself in 2018 and is determined to prove she can still rule Europe.

It is not quite 'master versus apprentice', but this is a fascinating next chapter when it comes to the balance of power in British sprinting - and it comes in the event each of them favour.

Asher-Smith has played down talk of a rivalry in the past, instead saying 'everyone is a rival' on the start line. But there is no doubt she will be determined to get one over her compatriot in one of the most intriguing head-to-heads this week.

Some fans picked up on the pair appearing to avoid each other following the conclusion of the women's 100m race in Birmingham.

Newly crowned 100m queen Amy Hunt, 24, is targeting her second gold of the week

Dina Asher-Smith, 30, is the big rival for Hunt in Thursday night's 200m final in Birmingham

Some fans picked up on the pair appearing to avoid each other after the 100m final

Asher-Smith missed out on a 100m medal but is out for revenge in the 200m final on Thursday

Athletics commentator Richard Newman alluded to the rivalry ahead of the Championships, saying on his Podium Athletics podcast: 'I do think - and I don't want to overhype the rivalry between them - but it's going to have so many more eyes on it.

'I think the media are going to build it up more. I think they're going to be asked about it a lot. I know it's real but the intensity of it could make it even more. The intensity of it is going to rise.'

Both domestic contenders eased to victories in their semi-finals and Hunt is staying zen ahead of the next chapter in her shot at history.

'I would give that a solid eight (out of ten),' she said. 'I knew I needed to put down a really hard turn, kill them to 150 (metres) and no-one was ever going to hang with me.

'I was trying to check the screens as I was in lane eight and figure out who was where to save a bit of energy for the final.

'To be relaxed and happy is the biggest thing. It's trying to stay social and not get yourself too serious as you can kill yourself doing that.

'I'm just trying to stay chill, my coach keeps me laughing and we have fun.'

The Cambridge University graduate's bubbly personality has endeared her to fans and brands alike, with sponsors reportedly queueing up to join forces with the 'relatable' star.

Her Instagram page, followed by 142,000 people, showcases her love of culture and literature as well as her exploits on the track, which have hit new heights since her breakthrough World Championship 200m gold in Tokyo last year.

She was not shy when broadcasting her aim to become the fastest woman in Europe, channelling her love of High School Musical when stating 'I want it all' at the start of the week.

The Newark athlete, who went to the same school in Grantham as Margaret Thatcher, now goes in search of following in Asher-Smith's footsteps with a 100m/200m European double.

Cambridge graduate Hunt's profile has boomed since she won silver in the 200m at last year's World Championships in Tokyo

Asher-Smith has been the queen of British sprinting since becoming world champion in 2019

She was made an MBE for her contribution to athletics in the New Year Honours last year

Asher-Smith was dethroned by her domestic rival over the shorter distance on Monday night but has won more European medals than any other Brit and another this evening would bring her tally to nine.

She finished fifth in the 100m but looked in ominous form in the 200m semis, cruising to victory in 22.49 seconds with plenty to spare.

'When you have so many motivated, talented and hard-working ladies, the important thing is a good lane draw for the final,' she said.

'I don't even know what number (medal) it is as to me every single one is different, every one comes in different circumstances.

'I don't really think about what's gone before or what lies ahead, I'm just trying to stay in the moment and execute.'

Two nights on from Romell Glave and Jeremiah Azu's one-two in the men's 100m, this is another domestic duel to savour for a home crowd.

After winning the 100m title at June's Novuna UK Athletics Championships on this track, Hunt said: 'It's so great. It shows that our national championships are one of the best in the world. Dina is one of the fastest athletes on the circuit, so I know I have to bring my A game.'

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"
